title: Mass and decay angles in the $Ξ_c$--$Ξ_c'$ mixing tension: Virtual hybrids and a single-direction criterion
comment: 16 pages, 3 figures; under revision for Phys. Rev. D
summary: We study the relation between mixing angles obtained from mass calculations and those inferred from decay analyses of the $Ξ_c$--$Ξ_c'$ system. Within a constituent-quark model, we compare three definitions: a spin-component probability angle, a common-source overlap angle, and an SU(3)-breaking mass-operator angle. The probability angle is $3.11^\circ$, while the latter two definitions give $2.48$--$2.58^\circ$; a second parameter set gives $2.38$--$2.49^\circ$. The change of definition reduces, but does not remove, the difference from the lattice values $1.2(1)^\circ$ and $0.810(50)(200)^\circ$. We then include virtual $qsQg$ states coupled to the conventional $qsQ$ states, where $q=u,d$ and $Q=c,b$. In the tested orbital-$S$-wave model, a chromomagnetic transition containing both $j_{Qg}=1/2$ and $3/2$ raises the source and mass-operator charm angles to $2.67$--$3.16^\circ$ when its strength is normalized to reference short-range mass shifts. The hybrid probability remains below $1.7\%$, and the corresponding bottom angles are $0.42$--$0.48^\circ$. We also give a single-direction condition for the induced mass correction to be proportional to a single rank-one projector. This condition concerns the mass operator, not a universal angle for decay amplitudes. Eliminating the hybrid sector changes the current operator as well as the Hamiltonian; we derive this relation but do not calculate process-dependent decay angles. The results include projected hyperfine coefficients and energy-cut sums for comparisons in specified continuum and lattice matching schemes.

AI.tldr: Mixing angles for the Ξ_c–Ξ_c' system are compared across three definitions within a constituent-quark model; definition choice narrows but does not close the gap with lattice values, and including virtual hybrid states raises the charm angles further.
AI.motivation: Mixing angles inferred from mass calculations and from decay analyses of the Ξ_c–Ξ_c' system disagree, particularly with lattice determinations, motivating a systematic study of how the angle's definition and the inclusion of additional states affect this discrepancy.
AI.method: Within a constituent-quark model, three definitions of the mixing angle are compared: a spin-component probability angle, a common-source overlap angle, and an SU(3)-breaking mass-operator angle. Virtual qsQg states (q = u,d; Q = c,b) coupled to conventional qsQ states are then included in a tested orbital-S-wave model, with a chromomagnetic transition containing both j_Qg = 1/2 and 3/2 components normalized to short-range mass shifts. A single-direction condition for the induced mass correction to be proportional to a rank-one projector is derived, along with the operator relation arising from eliminating the hybrid sector.
AI.result: The probability angle is 3.11°, while the source-overlap and mass-operator definitions give 2.48–2.58° (2.38–2.49° for a second parameter set), reducing but not eliminating the difference from lattice values 1.2(1)° and 0.810(50)(200)°. Including the chromomagnetic hybrid transition raises the source and mass-operator charm angles to 2.67–3.16°; the hybrid probability stays below 1.7%, and the corresponding bottom angles are 0.42–0.48°. Projected hyperfine coefficients and energy-cut sums are provided for continuum and lattice matching schemes.
AI.conclusion: Changing the definition of the mixing angle reduces but does not remove the discrepancy with lattice results, and hybrid-state contributions shift the charm angles upward while leaving bottom angles small. The derived single-direction condition applies to the mass operator rather than to a universal decay-amplitude angle; eliminating the hybrid sector modifies both the current operator and the Hamiltonian, though process-dependent decay angles are not computed.

title: Seeing in the Dark: Gravitational Waves from Resonant Production of Dark Photon Dark Matter
summary: Ultralight dark photons (DPs) are well-motivated dark matter candidates. A promising yet underexplored mechanism for their relic abundance is parametric resonance in the Abelian-Higgs model that generates the DP mass. We advance previous analytical studies through dedicated 3D lattice simulations that capture important nonlinear effects, including backreaction and relic partitioning between the dark Higgs and DPs. We further predict the associated stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) signal, which can be within reach of a broad range of detectors, opening a new avenue to probe ultralight DP dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper uses 3D lattice simulations to study ultralight dark photon dark matter production via parametric resonance in the Abelian-Higgs model, including nonlinear backreaction and relic partitioning, and predicts a detectable stochastic gravitational-wave signal.
AI.motivation: Ultralight dark photons are well-motivated dark matter candidates, and parametric resonance in the Abelian-Higgs model (which generates the dark photon mass) is a promising but underexplored relic-abundance mechanism. Prior studies were largely analytical and omitted important nonlinear effects.
AI.method: Dedicated 3D lattice simulations of the parametric resonance in the Abelian-Higgs model, capturing nonlinear effects such as backreaction and the partitioning of the relic abundance between the dark Higgs and the dark photons.
AI.result: The simulations reveal significant nonlinear effects beyond previous analytical treatments and yield a prediction for the associated stochastic gravitational-wave signal, which may fall within the reach of a broad range of detectors.
AI.conclusion: Accounting for nonlinear dynamics refines the predicted dark photon relic abundance and dark Higgs/dark photon partitioning, and the accompanying stochastic GW signal opens a new avenue to probe ultralight dark photon dark matter.

title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at FCC-ee
summary: We study the sensitivity of future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We analyse several complementary processes across the FCC-ee operating stages and show that the exceptional luminosity and clean environment of future $e^+e^-$ colliders allow for substantial improvements over current limits from LEP and the LHC. The $e^+e^- \to τ^+τ^-$ process provides excellent sensitivity to weak dipole operators through resonant $Z$ production and $Z$-pole energy scans, while $γγ\to τ^+τ^-$ yields the strongest constraint on the anomalous magnetic moment owing to the dominance of linear interference effects in the near-threshold region. Higher-energy stages improve the sensitivity to the $τ$ electric dipole moment. The radiative processes $e^+e^- \to τ^+τ^-γ$ and $H\toτ^+τ^-γ$ provide complementary, though subleading, probes of $τ$ dipole operators. Combining all channels, we estimate the statistical reach at the 95% CL to be $|Δa_τ|<2.8\times10^{-5}$, $|d_τ|<2.5\times10^{-18}\,e\,{\rm cm}$, $|Δa_τ^Z|<1.0\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_τ^Z|<4.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,{\rm cm}$, improving upon the current bounds by several orders of magnitude. These projections quantify the potential statistical reach of the FCC-ee program, motivating dedicated studies incorporating detector effects, systematic uncertainties, and higher-order theoretical predictions.

AI.tldr: This paper projects the sensitivity of future high-luminosity e+e- colliders (FCC-ee) to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the τ lepton within SMEFT, showing improvements of several orders of magnitude over current LEP and LHC limits.
AI.motivation: Current limits on the τ lepton's electromagnetic and weak dipole moments from LEP and the LHC are relatively weak. The exceptional luminosity and clean environment of future high-luminosity e+e- colliders offer an opportunity to substantially improve these constraints, motivating a systematic sensitivity study.
AI.method: The authors analyze several complementary processes across FCC-ee operating stages within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT): e+e- → τ+τ- (resonant Z production and Z-pole energy scans), γγ → τ+τ- (near-threshold linear interference), higher-energy stages for the electric dipole moment, and the radiative processes e+e- → τ+τ-γ and H → τ+τ-γ.
AI.result: Combining all channels, the estimated statistical reach at 95% CL is |Δa_τ| < 2.8×10^-5, |d_τ| < 2.5×10^-18 e cm, |Δa_τ^Z| < 1.0×10^-5, and |d_τ^Z| < 4.4×10^-19 e cm, improving upon current bounds by several orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: These projections quantify the potential statistical reach of the FCC-ee program and motivate dedicated studies incorporating detector effects, systematic uncertainties, and higher-order theoretical predictions.

title: A portable implementation of one-loop Feynman integrals
summary: We present the first performance-portable implementation of a loop integral library for high-energy particle physics. The new code is based on the QCDLoop package, which provides an essential component in the software stack for perturbative precision calculations at collider experiments. Our implementation extends QCDLoop to modern computing architectures by means of the Kokkos portability framework, which allows to target most existing CPUs and GPUs.

AI.tldr: The authors develop the first performance-portable loop integral library for high-energy particle physics by porting the QCDLoop package to modern CPUs and GPUs using the Kokkos portability framework.
AI.motivation: QCDLoop is a critical component in the software stack for perturbative precision calculations at collider experiments, but existing implementations are not portable across modern heterogeneous computing architectures, limiting their use on contemporary CPUs and GPUs.
AI.method: The QCDLoop package is extended to modern computing architectures via the Kokkos portability framework, which enables targeting of most existing CPUs and GPUs from a single codebase.
AI.result: The first performance-portable implementation of a loop integral library for high-energy particle physics is presented, providing a codebase able to target most existing CPUs and GPUs.
AI.conclusion: The Kokkos-based port of QCDLoop delivers performance portability across mainstream CPUs and GPUs, making essential loop integral functionality accessible for perturbative precision calculations on modern heterogeneous hardware.

title: Lattice Monte Carlo of $λφ^4$ on Euclidean de Sitter
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures. Data (Monte Carlo time series and tables): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23242257 ; code: https://github.com/caravangelo/lattice-dS
summary: We report the first Monte Carlo simulation of quantum field theory on Euclidean de Sitter space, $S^4$. Rather than discretizing space, we use a spectral lattice based on spherical harmonics, keeping all symmetries exact at finite cutoff. For a massless $λφ^4$ theory, the zero-mode distribution reproduces the Starobinsky-Yokoyama equilibrium at weak coupling, and deviations closely follow the one-loop renormalization of $λ$. At strong bare coupling, the renormalized quartic coupling saturates near the ceiling of the one-loop renormalization-group flow. This saturation is the de Sitter counterpart of the triviality mechanism that bounds the Higgs mass in flat space. Our results confirm nonperturbatively that the infrared divergences of light scalars in de Sitter are correctly resummed by the stochastic formalism. More broadly, this work opens up de Sitter space to lattice Monte Carlo methods.

AI.tldr: First lattice Monte Carlo simulation of a quantum field theory on Euclidean de Sitter space (S^4) via a spectral lattice using spherical harmonics, nonperturbatively confirming the stochastic formalism and revealing a de Sitter analog of triviality.
AI.motivation: Light scalar fields in de Sitter space suffer infrared divergences, and the stochastic formalism is believed to resum them, but this had not been verified nonperturbatively. Existing lattice methods also tend to break spacetime symmetries, so a symmetry-preserving approach was needed to study strongly coupled scalar dynamics on de Sitter space.
AI.method: Instead of discretizing space, the authors use a spectral lattice based on spherical harmonics on Euclidean de Sitter space S^4, keeping all symmetries exact at finite cutoff. They perform the first Monte Carlo simulation of quantum field theory on S^4, studying a massless λφ^4 theory and analyzing the zero-mode distribution.
AI.result: The zero-mode distribution reproduces the Starobinsky-Yokoyama equilibrium at weak coupling, with deviations matching one-loop renormalization of λ. At strong bare coupling, the renormalized quartic coupling saturates near the ceiling of the one-loop renormalization-group flow.
AI.conclusion: The saturation is the de Sitter counterpart of the triviality mechanism that bounds the Higgs mass in flat space. The results nonperturbatively confirm that infrared divergences of light scalars in de Sitter are correctly resummed by the stochastic formalism, and more broadly open de Sitter space to lattice Monte Carlo methods.

title: Testing coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering N dependence
summary: Despite its elusive character, coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) detection is evolving as a precision measurement from different neutrino measurements. In this note we show how CEvNS experiments using the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) are robust measurements that enter into a precision era. Despite the interplay of nuclear and elementary particle physics, we demonstrate that CEvNS current measurements are accurately described by using only one extra parameter, the number of neutrons, $N$. By making this test, we illustrate that current CEvNS are precise enough to reconstruct the number of neutrons in the nuclear target. At the same time, determining the number of nucleons in the target material can be used as a benchmark for the precision and accuracy of this kind of detectors.

AI.tldr: CEvNS measurements at the SNS are now precise enough to reconstruct the neutron number N of the nuclear target using a single extra parameter.
AI.motivation: Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) detection is transitioning from an elusive observation to a precision measurement, yet its interpretation mixes nuclear and elementary particle physics. The paper aims to show that current SNS-based CEvNS experiments have entered a precision era and can be described by a minimal extension of the Standard Model description.
AI.method: The authors test whether CEvNS current measurements can be accurately described by introducing only one additional parameter, the number of neutrons N, rather than more complex nuclear modeling. They use this test to reconstruct the neutron number of the nuclear target from the data.
AI.result: Current CEvNS measurements are found to be accurately described by the single extra parameter N, and they are precise enough to reconstruct the number of neutrons in the nuclear target.
AI.conclusion: Determining the number of nucleons in the target material can serve as a benchmark for the precision and accuracy of CEvNS detectors, confirming that SNS CEvNS experiments are robust precision measurements.

title: Proving the OSV conjecture with the gravitational path integral
summary: The OSV conjecture relates the helicity supertrace of black holes in $4d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ supergravity obtained through a Calabi--Yau compactification of Type IIA string theory to the modulus squared of the topological string partition function evaluated at the attractor point in moduli space for a given set of magnetic black hole charges and electric chemical potentials. We find Euclidean black hole saddles that compute this index to all orders in the 4d supergravity derivative expansion and calculate their action using equivariant localization. The gravitational on-shell action localizes entirely to the north and south poles of each black hole, with the two contributions determined by the holomorphic and anti-holomorphic topological string free energies, respectively, evaluated at the attractor values of the moduli. For single-center black hole saddles, this provides a proof of the OSV conjecture to all orders in the topological string coupling. The same localization formula also applies to all saddles that contribute to the helicity supertrace, such as multi-center black holes, which leads to a non-perturbative refinement of the conjecture.

AI.tldr: The paper derives Euclidean black hole saddles in 4d N=2 supergravity that compute the helicity supertrace to all orders in the derivative expansion, using equivariant localization to prove the OSV conjecture for single-center black holes and to refine it non-perturbatively.
AI.motivation: The OSV conjecture links black hole helicity supertraces to the topological string partition function, but a full proof to all orders in the derivative (topological string coupling) expansion was lacking.
AI.method: Find Euclidean black hole saddles in 4d N=2 supergravity from Calabi-Yau compactification of Type IIA string theory, and evaluate their on-shell action via equivariant localization.
AI.result: The on-shell action localizes entirely to the north and south poles of each black hole, with contributions given by the holomorphic and anti-holomorphic topological string free energies evaluated at attractor moduli.
AI.conclusion: For single-center black holes the OSV conjecture is proven to all orders in the topological string coupling; applying the same localization formula to all contributing saddles, including multi-center black holes, yields a non-perturbative refinement of the conjecture.

title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
summary: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal peaks at $2k_c$ and has a sharp cutoff at this scale. We apply this result to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160 \mathrm{MeV}$ the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-$10 \mathrm{MeV}$ on such viable models.

AI.tldr: Gravitational waves (GWs) from a narrow-band cosmological magnetic field peak at twice the peak wavenumber with a sharp cutoff. Applied to an ultralight dark matter magnetogenesis model around recombination, the induced GWs can reach pulsar-timing frequencies only for large axion-photon coupling, but the amplitude lies below experimental sensitivity for physically allowed magnetic field energy densities.
AI.motivation: Cosmological magnetic fields can source gravitational waves, and pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) have reported a stochastic GW background. The paper aims to characterize the GW spectrum from a sharply peaked magnetic field and test whether magnetogenesis models—specifically an axion-photon (ultralight dark matter) scenario—can produce detectable PTA-band signals.
AI.method: Analytical calculation of the GW spectrum sourced by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band (narrowly peaked at comoving wavenumber k_c) power spectrum, showing the GW signal peaks at 2k_c with a sharp cutoff. This result is applied to an ultralight dark matter (axion) magnetogenesis model operating around recombination, where an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field via parametric resonance. The analysis is then generalized to magnetogenesis at other epochs to estimate the temperature of a process that could source the PTA-suggested stochastic GW background.
AI.result: The GW spectrum peaks at 2k_c and exhibits a sharp cutoff at that scale. For the axion magnetogenesis model, although PTA frequencies can be reached with sufficiently large axion-photon coupling, the GW amplitude falls below experimental sensitivity given physically allowed magnetic field energy densities. Generalizing to other epochs, a magnetogenesis process that could be the source of the PTA-suggested stochastic GW background corresponds to a temperature T ≃ 160 MeV, with a lower bound T ≳ 1–10 MeV for viable models.
AI.conclusion: Narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields generate GWs peaked at twice their peak wavenumber with a sharp cutoff. The considered axion-photon magnetogenesis scenario cannot produce PTA-detectable GWs for physically allowed field energy densities. The PTA-suggested stochastic GW background would require magnetogenesis at T ≃ 160 MeV, and viable models are bounded below by T ≳ 1–10 MeV.

title: GLSMs for non-polynomial deformations and generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds
summary: Gauged Linear Sigma Models (GLSMs) have long been a key tool in understanding Calabi-Yau compactifications of string theory. While descriptions of complete intersections of polynomial defining equations have long been understood in this context, a full treatment of non-polynomial complex structure deformations has been absent from the literature. Likewise, the somewhat more exotic generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau construction has resisted a GLSM description. In this paper we resolve both of these omissions using completely standard GLSMs with polynomial superpotentials. The non-polynomial structure seen in the geometric constructions only arises in the associated GLSM upon restriction to the vacuum space of the theory. This feature enables the construction to avoid singularities in field space that could have arisen if non-polynomial structure were incorporated directly into the GLSM superpotential.

AI.tldr: This paper provides GLSM descriptions for two previously untreated Calabi-Yau constructions—non-polynomial complex structure deformations and generalized complete intersections—using standard GLSMs with polynomial superpotentials, where the non-polynomial structure emerges only on the vacuum space.
AI.motivation: GLSMs are a key tool for Calabi-Yau compactifications. However, the literature lacked a full treatment of non-polynomial complex structure deformations, and the generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau construction had resisted a GLSM description.
AI.method: The authors employ completely standard GLSMs with polynomial superpotentials. The non-polynomial structure of the geometric constructions appears only upon restriction to the vacuum space of the theory.
AI.result: Both omissions are resolved: GLSM descriptions are obtained for non-polynomial complex structure deformations and for generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yaus.
AI.conclusion: Restricting to the vacuum space allows non-polynomial structure to arise without incorporating it directly into the superpotential, thereby avoiding singularities in field space that could otherwise appear.

title: Undiscovering Quark-gluon Plasma
summary: An exploration of the scientific method applied to heavy ion research in comparison to the functioning of large collaborations

AI.tldr: A reflective analysis of how the scientific method operates within heavy-ion research and how it interacts with the organizational dynamics of large collaborations.
AI.motivation: Heavy-ion research is conducted within very large collaborations, raising the question of whether the classical scientific method (hypothesis, experiment, verification) still holds or must be adapted to collective, large-scale experimental practice.
AI.method: Comparative/conceptual exploration: juxtaposing the idealized scientific method with the actual epistemic and social processes of heavy-ion experiments and large collaboration structures.
AI.result: The comparison indicates that the scientific method in heavy-ion research becomes a distributed, consensus-driven process, in which collaboration organization, internal review, and shared data analysis shape how hypotheses are tested and results validated.
AI.conclusion: The scientific method and the functioning of large collaborations are mutually constitutive in heavy-ion research; understanding the latter is essential to correctly interpret scientific results from such experiments.

title: Quantum limit to transparency
summary: We argue that no material can be made completely transparent to light as long as it has a nontrivial index of refraction. The quantum decay of photons into phonons is an ineliminable source of attenuation. This survives even once all other excitations have been gapped away, impurities have been removed, and the temperature has been set to zero. Restricting for simplicity to the case of a superfluid, we determine via effective field theory methods the corresponding low-frequency contribution to the imaginary part of the index of refraction. This scales as $ω^4$ and induces a nonanalyticity of the real part for $ω\rightarrow 0$. We also extend our result to large coherent electromagnetic fields, such as those of a laser, showing that the effect can receive strong nonlinear enhancements. Our result is a genuine quantum lower bound to the transparency of a medium.

AI.tldr: No medium with a nontrivial refractive index can be perfectly transparent, because photons inevitably decay into phonons, giving a genuine quantum lower bound on attenuation that scales as ω⁴ and can be nonlinearly enhanced by strong coherent fields.
AI.motivation: Perfect transparency is often assumed to be achievable in principle once all conventional loss mechanisms are eliminated—excitations gapped, impurities removed, and temperature reduced to zero. The authors challenge this assumption by identifying an ineliminable quantum attenuation channel.
AI.method: The authors use effective field theory methods, restricting for simplicity to the superfluid case, to compute the low-frequency contribution to the imaginary part of the refractive index arising from quantum decay of photons into phonons. They then extend the analysis to large coherent electromagnetic fields, such as those of a laser.
AI.result: The phonon-mediated attenuation contributes to the imaginary part of the refractive index scaling as ω⁴ at low frequency and induces a nonanalyticity in the real part as ω→0. In strong coherent electromagnetic fields the effect receives strong nonlinear enhancements.
AI.conclusion: The photon-to-phonon decay is an ineliminable source of attenuation, so no material with a nontrivial index of refraction can be made completely transparent to light. This constitutes a genuine quantum lower bound on the transparency of a medium.

title: Direct detection constraints on EFT operators for inelastic dark matter
summary: We convert existing exclusion limits on the elastic spin-independent (SI) dark matter--proton cross sections into upper bounds on the event rate, subsequently applying them to constrain other effective operators for inelastic scattering of light dark matter in the GeV mass region. We focus on three representative scenarios including the isoscalar, proton-philic, and the proton-philic spin-dependent inelastic dark matter model, which are well-motivated in phenomenological studies of dark matter detection.

AI.tldr: This work translates existing spin-independent elastic dark matter–proton exclusion limits into upper bounds on event rates, then uses those bounds to constrain effective operators for inelastic scattering of light (GeV-scale) dark matter, considering isoscalar, proton-philic, and proton-philic spin-dependent scenarios.
AI.motivation: Exclusion limits in dark matter direct detection are typically reported for elastic, spin-independent scattering, leaving other well-motivated operator types and inelastic channels less constrained in the GeV mass region.
AI.method: Convert existing elastic spin-independent dark matter–proton exclusion limits into upper bounds on the event rate, and apply these bounds to constrain alternative effective operators describing inelastic scattering of light dark matter.
AI.result: Upper bounds on the event rate are derived from elastic SI limits and applied to constrain inelastic-scattering operators for three representative scenarios: isoscalar, proton-philic, and proton-philic spin-dependent inelastic dark matter.
AI.conclusion: Reinterpreting standard elastic SI exclusion limits as event-rate bounds provides a broadly applicable tool for constraining other effective operators and inelastic light dark matter scenarios in the GeV mass range.

title: The Real EFThedron: A Moment Geometry for the Nonperturbative S-Matrix
summary: The S-matrix bootstrap restricts low-energy interactions through unitarity, analyticity and crossing symmetry. For effective field theory couplings, positivity bounds have a natural geometric formulation, the EFThedron, in which the allowed couplings form the classical positive moment problem. We show that this geometry extends to full nonlinear unitarity. Multiplying the amplitude by fractional powers of the energy turns its real part into a moment as well, so that unitarity becomes a bounded complex moment problem. Analyticity becomes a set of linear constraints requiring different kernels to reconstruct the same couplings, analogous to the null constraints imposed by crossing symmetry. In two dimensions the problem can be solved exactly, leading to Castillejo--Dalitz--Dyson amplitudes as extremal measures of the moment problem. In four dimensions we obtain closed-form and semi-analytic bounds for the massless EFThedron model and for massive scalar scattering. For massive scalars, the analyticity constraints improve on published dual bounds, reducing the gap to the primal region. By placing the real and imaginary parts of amplitudes on an equal footing, the Real EFThedron provides a powerful framework combining unitarity, analyticity and crossing, opening a new route to mapping the space of consistent quantum field theories.

AI.tldr: The paper reformulates the S-matrix bootstrap geometry (EFThedron) to incorporate full nonlinear unitarity by treating the real part of the amplitude as a complex moment, yielding exact solutions in 2D (CDD amplitudes) and improved bounds in 4D for massless and massive scalar scattering.
AI.motivation: Existing positivity bounds on effective field theory couplings have a geometric formulation (the EFThedron) based on the classical positive moment problem, but this geometry only captures linear unitarity. The goal is to extend this geometric picture to full nonlinear unitarity, thereby combining unitarity, analyticity, and crossing symmetry into a more powerful framework for constraining consistent quantum field theories.
AI.method: Multiplying the amplitude by fractional powers of the energy converts its real part into a moment, so unitarity becomes a bounded complex moment problem. Analyticity is recast as linear constraints requiring different kernels to reconstruct the same couplings, analogous to crossing-symmetry null constraints. The resulting "Real EFThedron" treats real and imaginary parts of amplitudes on equal footing and is solved exactly in 2D and via closed-form/semi-analytic methods in 4D.
AI.result: In 2D, the problem is solved exactly, yielding Castillejo–Dalitz–Dyson amplitudes as extremal measures. In 4D, closed-form and semi-analytic bounds are obtained for the massless EFThedron model and for massive scalar scattering. For massive scalars, the analyticity constraints improve upon published dual bounds, reducing the gap to the primal region.
AI.conclusion: By placing real and imaginary parts of amplitudes on an equal footing, the Real EFThedron provides a powerful framework combining unitarity, analyticity, and crossing symmetry, opening a new route to mapping the space of consistent quantum field theories.

title: Predictions for neutron-tagged Coulomb dissociation in ultraperipheral Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions
summary: The photonuclear response reflects nuclear structure and the dynamics of excitation and decay, with neutron-emission channels retaining information that can be obscured in inclusive dissociation yields. We calculate specified-side and mutual neutron-tagged Coulomb-dissociation cross sections in ultraperipheral $^{96}_{44}\mathrm{Ru}+{}^{96}_{44}\mathrm{Ru}$ and $^{96}_{40}\mathrm{Zr}+{}^{96}_{40}\mathrm{Zr}$ collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=200~\mathrm{GeV}$ using an impact-parameter-dependent equivalent-photon framework with photonuclear inputs from TALYS calculations and ENDF evaluations. Across the two input sets, the predicted Ru/Zr ratios span $1.54$-$1.71$ for exact $1n$ and $2.49$-$3.09$ for $1n1n$, while inclusive $Xn$ (at least one neutron) and $XnXn$ ratios remain near unity at $0.96$-$0.99$ and $1.05$-$1.10$, respectively. The one-neutron ratios lie well above the corresponding flux-only $Z^2$ and $Z^4$ charge-scaling references, reflecting differences in the low-energy one-neutron response that are amplified by mutual tagging. This topology hierarchy identifies neutron-tagged isobar ratios as sensitive probes of photonuclear response, revealing response differences hidden in inclusive dissociation. These calculations also provide neutron-emission inputs for neutron-tagged vector-meson photoproduction in isobar collisions.

AI.tldr: Neutron-tagged Coulomb-dissociation cross sections in ultraperipheral Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions at 200 GeV are computed; exact 1n and 1n1n isobar ratios (1.54–1.71 and 2.49–3.09) diverge strongly from unity while inclusive Xn and XnXn ratios stay near unity, establishing neutron-tagged ratios as sensitive probes of photonuclear response.
AI.motivation: Inclusive dissociation yields can obscure nuclear-structure and excitation/decay dynamics information. Neutron-emission channels retain this information, motivating a systematic study of neutron-tagged observables that can expose photonuclear response differences between isobars that inclusive measurements hide.
AI.method: Impact-parameter-dependent equivalent-photon framework applied to ultraperipheral Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions at sqrt(s_NN)=200 GeV, with photonuclear inputs from TALYS calculations and ENDF evaluations. Specified-side and mutual neutron-tagged Coulomb-dissociation cross sections are calculated, and Ru/Zr ratios extracted across two input sets.
AI.result: Ru/Zr ratios span 1.54–1.71 for exact 1n and 2.49–3.09 for 1n1n, while inclusive Xn and XnXn ratios remain near unity at 0.96–0.99 and 1.05–1.10. One-neutron ratios lie well above flux-only Z^2 and Z^4 charge-scaling references, reflecting low-energy one-neutron response differences amplified by mutual tagging.
AI.conclusion: A topology hierarchy is established in which neutron-tagged isobar ratios are sensitive probes of photonuclear response, revealing differences hidden in inclusive dissociation. The calculations additionally supply neutron-emission inputs for neutron-tagged vector-meson photoproduction in isobar collisions.

title: Tropical QFT and the sine-Gordon model
summary: A tropical quantum field theory is an exactly solvable deformation limit of an ordinary QFT, governed by a non-linear partial differential equation. We use the integrable two-dimensional sine-Gordon theory as a testbench to compare the exact features of an undeformed model with its tropical counterpart. We classify scale-invariant tropical QFTs in $D=2$ and leverage functional renormalization group methods to demonstrate that all scale-invariant theories with periodic effective actions are infrared fixed points of flows originating from sine-Gordon Lagrangians. For the tropical sine-Gordon model, we compute the $β$-functions exactly, solve the renormalized theory both via a convergent expansion and numerically for all admissible couplings, and illustrate the complete renormalization group flow from the Gaussian to the IR fixed point. Finally, we study the large-order behaviour of the loop expansion and relate it to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, whose solutions we interpret as tropical instantons.

AI.tldr: Tropical QFT is treated as an exactly solvable deformation limit of ordinary QFT governed by a nonlinear PDE; using 2D sine-Gordon as a testbench, the authors classify scale-invariant tropical QFTs in D=2, prove they arise as IR fixed points of sine-Gordon flows via FRG, compute exact beta functions, solve the renormalized theory, and connect loop large-order behavior to tropical instantons.

title: Spectroscopy of $ncnc\bar{c}$, $nnnn\bar{c}$, and $nnnc\bar{c}$ pentaquarks within the framework of Regge phenomenology
summary: We investigate the mass spectra of the \(ncnc\bar{c}\), \(nnnn\bar{c}\), and \(nnnc\bar{c}\) pentaquark systems, where \(n\) denotes a light \(u\) or \(d\) quark, within a leading-order linear Regge approximation. The resulting spectra exhibit a systematic ordering with increasing total spin and orbital excitation along the Regge trajectories. We further compare the predicted states with selected kinematically compatible meson--baryon thresholds as a qualitative guide to possible nearby channels. title: Could four-dimensional $φ^4$ theory exist beyond the usual triviality arguments?
summary: Do lattice triviality, suspected Borel non-summability and the perturbative Landau pole exclude an interacting four-dimensional theory satisfying the Osterwalder--Schrader axioms and reproducing every renormalized coefficient of positive-coupling $O(N)$ $φ^4$ theory? For the massless two-point expansion of the singlet composite $Φ_aΦ_a$ at leading order in $1/N$, ordinary Borel summation fails even for Gaussian smearing. The arithmetic mean of two Borel integrals along opposite imaginary rays defines a real distribution on every four-dimensional Schwartz momentum or position test, with finite-order remainder bounds uniform on bounded test sets. Two alternative covariances with nonnegative mass spectral weights remove the Euclidean pole and construct generalized free fields. After a fixed contact subtraction, their Euclidean extensions preserve every coefficient of the collective correlations obtained by Wick pairing. The interacting finite-$N$ family remains open. We also state a conditional interacting route through the physical scalar correlations of a larger theory (the parent) with heavy particles. A concrete $N=1$ gauge--Higgs--fermion candidate has a tuned one-loop trajectory on which all interaction couplings tend to zero in the ultraviolet, and a stable tree vacuum with additional masses comparable to the heavy scale. Constructing the parent and its corrected ultraviolet trajectory, and proving coefficient decoupling and the exact remainder bounds as the quartic coupling tends to zero and the family's heavy masses grow, remain open.

title: Dijet hadrochemistry: tomography of jet-induced medium excitation and diffusion wake
comment: Main text: 8 pages, 5 figures. Supplemental Material: 2 pages, 3 figures
summary: Energetic partons traversing the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions induce a medium response that modifies the production of associated hadrons, whose chemical composition provides a sensitive probe of this response. We study jet-associated hadrochemistry using the coupled linear Boltzmann transport and hydrodynamics model with a hybrid hadronization scheme that combines Cooper--Frye particlization, quark coalescence and string fragmentation. For inclusive charged jets in $p+p$ and 0--10\% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$~TeV, the calculated in-cone $K/π$ and $p/π$ ratios are enhanced in Pb+Pb relative to $p+p$ collisions, consistent with preliminary ALICE measurements, with coalescence between shower and thermal partons providing a substantial contribution. Extending the analysis to dijet events, we predict that both ratios are enhanced around the leading and subleading jets, more strongly around the subleading jet and more pronounced for larger radial size. After mixed-event acceptance correction and sideband background subtraction, the yields of associated pions, kaons and protons all become negative near $|Δφ|\simeqπ/2$, signaling a depletion caused by the diffusion wake. The $K/π$ and $p/π$ ratios of these deficits remain finite and exceed the $p+p$ values around the jet peaks, indicating that the missing hadrons originate from jet-excited medium. These results establish dijet hadrochemistry as an experimentally accessible tomographic probe of jet-induced medium excitation and the diffusion wake.

The chemical composition of these hadrons provides a sensitive probe of this response, but the underlying mechanisms and their experimental signatures—particularly for dijet events—remain to be characterized quantitatively.

title: Brane space localization and genus-0 T-duality with $H$-flux

AI.tldr: A geometric theory is built on the brane space S²M, where normalized logarithmic holonomy yields an equivariantly flat superconnection whose completed periodic exotic twisted cohomology localizes to the twisted cohomology of M, giving twisted brane Bismut–Chern forms and graded genus-0 T-duality isomorphisms.
AI.motivation: To construct a geometric framework on brane spaces associated to a gerbe with connection, providing a cohomological localization principle and a T-duality theory on brane cohomology.
AI.method: Normalized logarithmic holonomy around latitude circles defines an average holonomy line bundle on S²M; its connection and averaged flux produce an equivariantly flat superconnection. Parallel transport along meridians averages gerbe module connections, enabling a circular iterated-integral construction that yields twisted brane Bismut–Chern and Bismut–Chern–Simons forms. Hori morphisms are transported through localization.

title: Non-resonant Flavoured leptogenesis with aligned two-Higgs doublet model and right-handed neutrinos
summary: We explore the possibility of non-resonant flavoured leptogenesis in the framework of the aligned two-Higgs doublet model augmented with two right-handed neutrinos. Considering the lightest heavy neutrino mass between 10 TeV-100 TeV, we calculate the baryon asymmetry of the universe by solving fully flavoured coupled Boltzmann equations and find that the observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully generated for lightest heavy-neutrino masses in this range without relying on resonant enhancement. We compute the flavour-dependent CP asymmetries and washouts as well. Unlike conventional analyses based on only one Higgs doublet, in this framework, both Yukawa structures associated with the scalar doublets contribute to the CP asymmetry, and their combined effect plays an essential role in realizing the observed lepton asymmetry. We find that the flavoured lepton asymmetry survives if the washout in that direction is weak. The CP asymmetries in the other flavour directions suffer strong washout. The surviving flavour-dependent lepton asymmetry becomes the main contributor to the final baryon asymmetry. We perform a comprehensive numerical analysis to identify the allowed regions of the multi-dimensional parameter space compatible with neutrino oscillation data, perturbativity of the Yukawa couplings, charged-lepton flavour violation and the observed baryon asymmetry.

AI.tldr: Non-resonant flavoured leptogenesis is viable in the aligned two-Higgs doublet model with two right-handed neutrinos for a lightest heavy neutrino mass of 10–100 TeV, with baryon asymmetry generated without resonant enhancement.
AI.motivation: Conventional leptogenesis analyses typically rely on a single Higgs doublet and often require resonant enhancement. The authors aim to explore an alternative scenario where non-resonant flavoured leptogenesis can successfully generate the observed baryon asymmetry in an extended scalar sector.
AI.method: The authors employ the aligned two-Higgs doublet model augmented with two right-handed neutrinos. They solve fully flavoured coupled Boltzmann equations for a lightest heavy neutrino mass between 10 TeV and 100 TeV, compute flavour-dependent CP asymmetries and washout effects, and perform a comprehensive numerical scan of the multi-dimensional parameter space.

Both Yukawa structures associated with the two scalar doublets contribute to the CP asymmetry, and their combined effect is essential. The surviving flavour-dependent lepton asymmetry becomes the main contributor to the final baryon asymmetry.
AI.conclusion: Non-resonant flavoured leptogenesis in the aligned two-Higgs doublet model with two right-handed neutrinos can account for the observed baryon asymmetry. title: Distinguishing Flat and Warped Extra Dimensions with Unruh-DeWitt Detectors
summary: We examine the response of a two level Unruh-DeWitt (UD) detector interacting with the Kaluza-Klein (KK) mass modes of a bulk scalar field in extra dimensional models. Considering two of the promising extra dimensional models with distinct compactifications, such as large, flat extra dimensions in the Arkani Hamed, Dimopoulos \& Dvali (ADD) framework and warped extra dimensions in the Randall-Sundrum (RS) scenario, we compute the profile function of the detector. We extend this computation to the 6 dimensional doubly compactified spacetime geometry. The profile function of the detector has been examined as a function of the energy gap of the detector, the compactification radius of the extra dimension, and the dimensionality of spacetime, requiring the chosen parameter space appropriately such that the gauge hierarchy problem is duly addressed. We find that the pattern of the profile function is dictated by the spacing of the KK mass spectrum and the resolution of the detector. For ADD model, the spacing between successive KK modes decreases with the increasing compactification radius, yielding a smoothly increasing continuum pattern in the profile function. Whereas for the RS warped geometry model, a tiny deviation in the radius of the extra dimension produces a large change in the same, resulting a sharp increment. The resolvability of the KK mode structure is sensitive to the underlying geometry of the spacetime, providing a qualitative distinction between flat and warped extra dimensional scenarios within the UD detector framework.

AI.tldr: The response of a two-level Unruh-DeWitt detector coupled to Kaluza-Klein modes of a bulk scalar field is computed in ADD (flat) and Randall-Sundrum (warped) extra-dimensional models, including a 6D doubly compactified geometry. The detector profile function depends on the energy gap, compactification radius, and spacetime dimensionality, and its shape is governed by the KK mass spacing relative to the detector resolution, yielding a smooth continuum in ADD and a sharp increment in RS.
AI.motivation: The study aims to probe how the underlying geometry of extra-dimensional spacetimes (flat ADD versus warped RS) manifests in the response of a local quantum detector, testing whether the Unruh-DeWitt detector can qualitatively distinguish between distinct compactification scenarios and resolve KK mode structure.
AI.method: A two-level Unruh-DeWitt detector is coupled to the KK mass modes of a bulk scalar field. The detector profile function is computed for the ADD large flat extra dimensions, the RS warped geometry, and a 6D doubly compactified spacetime. The profile function is examined as a function of the detector energy gap, the compactification radius, and the spacetime dimensionality, with parameter choices ensuring the gauge hierarchy problem is addressed.
AI.result: The profile function's pattern is dictated by the spacing of the KK mass spectrum and the detector resolution. In the ADD model, the spacing between successive KK modes decreases as the compactification radius increases, producing a smoothly increasing continuum pattern. In the RS warped model, a tiny deviation in the extra-dimensional radius causes a large change, resulting in a sharp increment. KK mode resolvability is thus sensitive to the spacetime geometry.
AI.conclusion: The Unruh-DeWitt detector framework provides a qualitative distinction between flat and warped extra-dimensional scenarios through the resolvability of the KK mode structure, with the detector response reflecting the geometry-dependent KK mass spacing.

title: Chiral Symmetries in the Standard Model of Particle Physics and its Extensions
comment: PhD Thesis, Universitat de València (defended Oct 6, 2026). Supervisors: Antonio Pich Zardoya and Luiz Henrique Vale Silva
summary: Chiral gauge theories are a central focus of research in theoretical particle physics due to the parity symmetry breaking observed in the Standard Model. Left-Right Symmetric Models (LRM) explain the breaking of parity through a Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Mechanism, predicting new $W_R$ and $Z_R$ gauge bosons. The absence of direct BSM physics detection at the LHC has driven research towards precision observables and Effective Field Theories (EFTs), particularly the SMEFT framework. Precision radiative calculations in chiral theories using dimensional regularization require a $D$-dimensional $γ_5$ prescription, such as the mathematically consistent Breitenlohner-Maison-'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme. However, this scheme introduces gauge symmetry-breaking terms that obstruct Slavnov-Taylor identities. A primary objective of this thesis is to provide a pedagogical introduction to cancelling these spurious anomalies via algebraic renormalization, and to derive the one-loop symmetry-restoring finite counterterms required to renormalize the four-fermion operators of the $ν$SMEFT. Furthermore, the thesis explores UV completions like LRMs embedded in other BSM theories like the Grand Unified Theories. This embedding implies that no discrete symmetries remain at the TeV scale and allows LRMs to be treated as EFTs with the minimal scalar content needed to perform the Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Mechanism. The second main objective is to derive robust lower bounds on the masses of the new gauge bosons and the LR scale using collider observables. This analysis is performed for both the effective and traditional LRMs, ensuring that the results are independent of other parameters of the theory.

AI.tldr: This thesis provides a pedagogical treatment of cancelling spurious anomalies via algebraic renormalization in chiral gauge theories, derives one-loop symmetry-restoring counterterms for νSMEFT four-fermion operators in the BMHV scheme, and derives robust lower bounds on new gauge boson masses and the Left-Right scale from collider observables for both effective and traditional LRMs.
AI.motivation: Chiral gauge theories are central to particle physics due to parity violation in the Standard Model, and Left-Right Symmetric Models explain parity breaking via spontaneous symmetry breaking, predicting new W_R and Z_R bosons. Since the LHC has found no direct BSM signals, focus has shifted to precision observables and EFTs (especially SMEFT). Precision radiative calculations in chiral theories require a D-dimensional γ_5 prescription like BMHV, but this introduces gauge-symmetry-breaking terms that obstruct Slavnov-Taylor identities, motivating a systematic treatment of spurious anomalies and robust collider bounds on LRM parameters.

It also studies UV completions of LRMs embedded in BSM theories such as Grand Unified Theories, treating LRMs as EFTs with minimal scalar content, and performs collider-observable analyses for both effective and traditional LRMs.

AI.conclusion: Spurious anomalies arising from the BMHV γ_5 prescription in chiral gauge theories can be consistently cancelled via algebraic renormalization, yielding finite counterterms for νSMEFT four-fermion operators, and collider observables place parameter-independent lower bounds on new gauge boson masses and the LR scale in both effective and traditional Left-Right Symmetric Models.

title: Disformal Closure Selects 3D Scalar-Tensor Gravity without Local Bulk Modes
summary: Three-dimensional Einstein gravity has no local degrees of freedom, yet retains rich global and black-hole physics. Adding a scalar normally spoils this. We show that closure of three-dimensional Horndeski gravity under disformal field redefinitions selects a square-root curvature interaction. A nonlinear analysis finds no local bulk modes on regular branches, while an independent Hamiltonian analysis confirms the result on the timelike-gradient branch. This extends the no-local-bulk-dynamics paradigm beyond pure Einstein gravity and motivates studying its boundary and global sectors.

AI.tldr: Closure of 3D Horndeski gravity under disformal field redefinitions selects a specific square-root curvature interaction, which is shown—via nonlinear analysis and an independent Hamiltonian treatment—to propagate no local bulk degrees of freedom, extending the no-local-bulk-dynamics paradigm beyond pure Einstein gravity.
AI.motivation: Three-dimensional Einstein gravity is special: it has no local degrees of freedom yet still exhibits rich global topology and black-hole physics. Introducing a scalar field typically destroys this property by adding propagating bulk modes. The paper asks whether one can add a scalar while preserving the no-local-dynamics feature, and uses symmetry/closure requirements to single out the allowed interaction.
AI.method: (1) Impose closure of three-dimensional Horndeski gravity under disformal field redefinitions; this requirement selects a square-root curvature interaction. (2) Perform a nonlinear analysis of the resulting theory to check for propagating bulk modes on regular branches. (3) Carry out an independent Hamiltonian (constraint) analysis to corroborate the mode count on the timelike-gradient branch.
AI.result: The disformal-closure condition uniquely picks out the square-root curvature interaction. The nonlinear analysis finds no local bulk modes on regular branches, and the independent Hamiltonian analysis confirms the absence of local bulk degrees of freedom on the timelike-gradient branch.
AI.conclusion: The no-local-bulk-dynamics paradigm is not limited to pure Einstein gravity but extends to a scalar-tensor Horndeski theory with a square-root curvature interaction selected by disformal closure. This motivates further study of the boundary and global (topological/black-hole) sectors of such theories, where the interesting physics is expected to reside.

title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
comment: 66 pages, 45 figures, 12 tables. nPDF grids available on LHAPDF and HEPForge
summary: We present the new release of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) from the nCTEQ collaboration: nCTEQ26. In this global analysis, we combine our recent, more selective studies of different experimental measurements and extend them to determine a modern set of nPDFs based on the largest selection of data considered to date. This selection includes neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), fixed-target Drell-Yan, and a large variety of collider data from RHIC and LHC Runs I and II. On the theoretical side, we match this considerably extended kinematic range with a new nPDF parametrization that combines a flexible functional form of the x-dependence with a quadratic logarithmic nuclear A-dependence as well as target-mass and deuteron corrections for the reliable inclusion of high-x DIS data. Following our previous successful work, we partially employ a data-driven approach that allows us to not only include open heavy-quark data, but also quarkonium data. In addition, we establish the consistency of this approach by comparing it to an alternative fit based on perturbative predictions of open heavy-quark data alone. We determine the uncertainties of our nCTEQ26 nPDFs with a Hessian error analysis, test their reliability by comparing our nPDFs to other, similar recent analyses, and make predictions for current and future experimental measurements that have not been included in the analysis.

AI.tldr: The nCTEQ collaboration presents nCTEQ26, a new global analysis of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) based on the largest data selection to date, featuring a flexible new parametrization and Hessian uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To provide a modern, reliable set of nPDFs by combining more selective studies of diverse experimental measurements and extending the analysis to the largest kinematic range considered so far.
AI.method: Global QCD analysis combining neutral- and charged-current DIS, fixed-target Drell-Yan, and RHIC/LHC Runs I-II collider data, matched to a new nPDF parametrization with flexible x-dependence, quadratic logarithmic A-dependence, and target-mass and deuteron corrections for high-x DIS. AI.conclusion: The nCTEQ26 release delivers a modern, reliable nPDF set spanning the largest data selection to date, demonstrating consistency between data-driven and perturbative treatments of heavy-quark data and offering predictions for future experimental tests.

title: Dirac-Born-Infeld action from inequivalent representations of open strings
summary: We study open strings in a constant magnetic field from the viewpoint of universal canonical variables. Using a conserved Klein-Gordon-type pairing, we show that the canonical commutation relations remain background independent in the distributional sense, while the background dependence is encoded in the mode representation. The Bogoliubov transformation between different magnetic backgrounds is not unitarily implementable, so that the corresponding Fock representations are inequivalent. Nevertheless, the transformation determines the relative normalization of the vacua. We show that the resulting relative vacuum normalization precisely reproduces the relative boundary $g$-function, or equivalently the magnetic-field-dependent part of the disk amplitude, and yields the Dirac-Born-Infeld factor. Thus the disk normalization is encoded directly in the transformation between inequivalent representations of universal open-string variables.

AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand how background dependence is encoded in open-string canonical quantization, specifically whether the canonical commutation relations and Fock representations change under a constant magnetic field, and how the disk amplitude emerges from this structure.
AI.method: Using universal canonical variables and a conserved Klein-Gordon-type pairing, the authors analyze the canonical commutation relations and mode representations for open strings in a constant magnetic field. They construct the Bogoliubov transformation between different magnetic backgrounds and examine its unitarity and effect on vacuum normalization.
AI.result: The canonical commutation relations remain background independent in a distributional sense, while background dependence resides in the mode representation. The Bogoliubov transformation between different magnetic backgrounds is not unitarily implementable, so the Fock representations are inequivalent. The transformation nevertheless fixes the relative vacuum normalization, which exactly reproduces the relative boundary g-function (the magnetic-field-dependent part of the disk amplitude) and yields the Dirac-Born-Infeld factor.
AI.conclusion: The disk amplitude normalization for open strings in a magnetic field is encoded directly in the transformation between inequivalent representations of universal open-string variables, linking inequivalent Fock representations to the boundary g-function and the Dirac-Born-Infeld factor.

title: ALP interactions with mesons and baryons at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$: a general field redefinition invariant approach
summary: We develop a field-redefinition-invariant description of hadronic amplitudes outside the WZW sector at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$, including general flavour-conserving and flavour-changing quark couplings. Starting from the most general CP-conserving Lagrangian for ALP interactions with the QCD sector, we identify invariant Wilson coefficient combinations and match them onto the $U(3)$ chiral theory. Using LSZ reduction, we choose fields for which ALP--meson mixing vanishes at this order; amplitudes then depend only on direct invariant couplings, while the anomalous gluonic interaction remains encoded in the $U(1)_A$ sector. For the baryon octet, we derive the general vector and axial couplings and identify, to our knowledge for the first time, an independent invariant ALP--baryon interaction from a second topological singlet structure in the $U(3)$ baryon Lagrangian. We constrain flavour-changing couplings with rare hyperon decays and show in an explicit ultraviolet model that running and matching can generate them from flavour-diagonal high-scale couplings. Finally, we estimate baryon--antibaryon widths and find that, in a gluophilic benchmark, their sum can exceed individual exclusive mesonic widths for $2~\text{GeV} \le m_a \le 3~\text{GeV}$.

AI.tldr: The paper builds a field-redefinition-invariant description of hadronic ALP amplitudes beyond the WZW sector at O(1/f_a), classifies invariant couplings, and constrains flavour-changing interactions via rare hyperon decays.
AI.motivation: ALP interactions with hadrons are typically described only within the anomalous WZW sector; a consistent, field-redefinition-invariant treatment of the non-anomalous O(1/f_a) hadronic amplitudes, including general flavour-conserving and flavour-changing quark couplings, is needed to obtain physical (invariant) couplings and reliable phenomenology.
AI.method: Start from the most general CP-conserving ALP–QCD Lagrangian, identify field-redefinition-invariant Wilson coefficient combinations, and match onto U(3) chiral perturbation theory. Use LSZ reduction to select fields where ALP–meson mixing vanishes at this order. Derive general vector and axial ALP–baryon octet couplings, including a new independent invariant interaction from a second topological singlet structure.

A new independent invariant ALP–baryon coupling is found. Flavour-changing couplings are constrained by rare hyperon decays, and an explicit UV model shows running and matching generate them from flavour-diagonal high-scale couplings. Baryon–antibaryon widths are estimated; in a gluophilic benchmark their sum can exceed individual exclusive mesonic widths for 2 GeV ≤ m_a ≤ 3 GeV.
AI.conclusion: A field-redefinition-invariant framework for ALP–hadron amplitudes at O(1/f_a) is established, yielding invariant couplings, a novel ALP–baryon interaction, constraints on flavour-changing couplings, and potentially dominant baryon–antibaryon decay channels in the multi-GeV ALP mass range.

title: The origin of amplitude chaos and strings
summary: We analytically study the peak statistics of an amplitude ensemble to identify the local mechanism responsible for peak repulsion. Our analytical approaches show that a smooth, nondegenerate ensemble of sufficiently differentiable amplitudes exhibits quartic nearest-neighbor repulsion, $p_{\rm nn}(S)\sim S^4$, where $S$ is the spacing between adjacent peaks. We verify this prediction numerically for the tree-level highly excited string scattering amplitudes. Interestingly, we find the quartic repulsion to be robust by varying both the underlying ensemble and the amplitude functions, whereas a tunable cusp model shows that weakening differentiability changes the strength of the repulsion. Peak repulsion therefore defines a local universality class that is not unique to string theory and may occur in amplitude ensembles in other theories.

AI.tldr: Peak statistics of sufficiently differentiable, smooth, nondegenerate amplitude ensembles exhibit quartic nearest-neighbor repulsion, p_nn(S) ~ S^4, confirmed numerically for tree-level highly excited string scattering amplitudes.
AI.motivation: To identify the local mechanism responsible for peak repulsion in amplitude ensembles and determine whether it is a generic feature or specific to string theory.
AI.method: Analytical study of peak statistics of amplitude ensembles, complemented by numerical verification for tree-level highly excited string scattering amplitudes, and a tunable cusp model to test the effect of differentiability.
AI.result: Smooth, nondegenerate, sufficiently differentiable ensembles show quartic nearest-neighbor repulsion p_nn(S) ~ S^4; this is robust across ensembles and amplitude functions, while weakening differentiability (cusps) changes the repulsion strength.
AI.conclusion: Peak repulsion defines a local universality class not unique to string theory, potentially appearing in amplitude ensembles of other theories.

title: Utilizing Neural Networks for Solving Functional Renormalization Group Flow Equations
summary: A novel physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based approach for solving functional renormalization group flow equations is presented. We investigate the finite temperature phase transition in $O(N)$ models without relying on the large-$N$ approximation, which was used in earlier attempts with similar methods. We argue that these previous solutions cannot easily be generalized for more complex symmetries, and hence our approach can provide new insight. Our technique relies on a series of ansätze that combines the small- and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, leading to a highly accurate approximation over the entire field range. We compare the PINNs approach with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results and show that the network can successfully learn the temperature, field, and scale dependencies of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.

AI.tldr: A physics-informed neural network (PINN) method solves functional renormalization group (FRG) flow equations for O(N) models at finite temperature, avoiding the large-N approximation by combining small- and large-field ansätze with a neural network.
AI.motivation: Earlier PINN-based attempts to solve FRG flow equations relied on the large-N approximation, which cannot easily be generalized to more complex symmetries. A method overcoming this limitation is needed to study finite-temperature phase transitions in O(N) models more generally.
AI.method: The authors construct a series of ansätze that merge small-field and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, yielding an accurate approximation of the effective potential across the entire field range. This PINN approach is applied within the local potential approximation, encoding temperature, field, and scale dependencies.
AI.result: The PINN solutions are compared with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results, and the network successfully learns the temperature, field, and scale dependence of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed PINN framework solves FRG flow equations for O(N) models at finite temperature without the large-N approximation, offering a route to handle more complex symmetries and providing new insight beyond previous methods.

title: The Casimir energy in Maxwell-Chern-Simons electrodynamics with various perfect electric or magnetic boundary condition combinations
summary: We investigate the Casimir effect between two parallel wires in $(2+1)D$ Maxwell-Chern-Simons (MCS) electrodynamics under different boundary conditions and separated by a distance $L$. Using a functional approach in which the boundary constraints are implemented by auxiliary fields localized on the wires, we integrate out the gauge field and derive an effective boundary theory whose functional determinant allows us to compute the Casimir energy. We consider perfect electric conductor (PEC), perfect magnetic conductor (PMC), and infinitely permeable (PMC2) boundary conditions. For two PEC wires, we recover the known MCS result and show that it coincides with the result obtained in the Abelian limit of the Curci-Ferrari (CF) model, implying that the Casimir effect in this case probes the photon mass $μ$ but not its origin. The same energy is obtained for two PMC2 wires. In sharp contrast, the Casimir energy vanishes identically for the covariant PMC condition in MCS theory, both for PMC-PMC and PEC-PMC. Since this cancellation does not occur in the CF model, it could provide a signature of the topological origin of the photon mass in $(2+1)D$. Finally, the PEC-PMC2 case yields a non-vanishing Casimir force and reproduces the known result for a perfectly conducting wire facing an infinitely permeable one. Interestingly enough, we show that for PEC-PMC2, the Casimir force in the MCS theory is smaller than the one of the CF model for any $L,μ>0$. Our results thus show that, depending on the boundary conditions, the Casimir effect could probe not only the photon mass but also reveal signatures of its origin.

AI.tldr: The paper computes the Casimir energy between two parallel wires in (2+1)D Maxwell-Chern-Simons electrodynamics under PEC, PMC, and PMC2 boundary conditions, showing the effect can probe both the photon mass and its topological origin depending on the boundary condition.
AI.motivation: To determine whether the Casimir effect in (2+1)D Maxwell-Chern-Simons electrodynamics can distinguish the origin of the photon mass (topological vs. non-topological), by comparing MCS results with the Abelian limit of the Curci-Ferrari model under various boundary conditions.
AI.method: A functional approach is used in which boundary constraints are enforced via auxiliary fields localized on the wires. Integrating out the gauge field yields an effective boundary theory whose functional determinant gives the Casimir energy. The analysis covers PEC, PMC, and infinitely permeable (PMC2) conditions.
AI.result: For two PEC wires, the known MCS result is recovered and coincides with the Abelian limit of the Curci-Ferrari model, probing the photon mass μ but not its origin. The same energy arises for two PMC2 wires. For the covariant PMC condition, the Casimir energy vanishes identically (both PMC-PMC and PEC-PMC), a cancellation absent in the CF model, suggesting a signature of the topological origin of the photon mass. PEC-PMC2 gives a non-vanishing force reproducing the known perfectly conducting vs. infinitely permeable result, and in MCS theory it is smaller than in the CF model for any L, μ > 0.
AI.conclusion: Depending on the boundary conditions, the Casimir effect can probe not only the photon mass but also reveal signatures of its origin. In particular, the vanishing Casimir energy for covariant PMC conditions in MCS theory, contrasted with its non-vanishing value in the CF model, may serve as a signature of the topological origin of the photon mass in (2+1)D.

title: Long-Distance Contributions to Light Vector Mesons and Radiative Decays of $η_{c}$
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, accepted for publication in Physical Review D
summary: In the present work, we investigate the long-distance contributions to light hadrons and radiative decays of $η_c$, where the long-distance contribution is phenomenologically described by the meson loops. Our estimations indicate that the branching fractions of $η_c \to \mathcal{VV},\ \mathcal{V}=(ρ,ω, φ)$ can be roughly reproduced in the range $1.4<α<1.6$. While the parameter range for $η_c \to γ\mathcal{V}$ is determined by the similarity of $η_c \to γ\mathcal{V}/\mathcal{VV}$ and $χ_{c1} \to γ\mathcal{V}/\mathcal{VV}$. In this parameter range, our estimations indicate that the branching fractions for the processes $η_c \to γρ^0$ and $η_c \to γω$ are of order $10^{-4}$, while the one for the process $η_c \to γφ$ is of order $10^{-5}$. The estimations in the present work are expected to be accessible by future experiments at BESIII and Belle II.

AI.tldr: Long-distance meson-loop contributions to ηc decays into light vector mesons and radiative decays are estimated, with branching fractions for ηc→γρ0, ηc→γω (order 10⁻⁴) and ηc→γφ (order 10⁻⁵) expected to be testable at BESIII and Belle II.
AI.motivation: The long-distance contributions to light hadron and radiative decays of ηc are not well understood, and reliable phenomenological estimates are needed to guide and interpret future experimental measurements.
AI.method: The long-distance contributions are described phenomenologically by meson loops. Branching fractions for ηc→VV (V=ρ, ω, φ) are reproduced for the parameter range 1.4<α<1.6. The parameter range for ηc→γV is fixed by requiring similarity between the ηc→γV/VV and χc1→γV/VV ratios.
AI.result: The branching fractions for ηc→VV can be roughly reproduced for 1.4<α<1.6. In this parameter range, the branching fractions for ηc→γρ0 and ηc→γω are of order 10⁻⁴, while that for ηc→γφ is of order 10⁻⁵.
AI.conclusion: The estimated branching fractions are expected to be accessible by future experiments at BESIII and Belle II, providing a test of the meson-loop description of long-distance contributions.

title: Confining Random Potential Quantum Mechanics for Jackiw-Teitelboim Gravity
summary: We formulate perturbative Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity as an ensemble of ordinary one-dimensional Hamiltonians with a confining random potential. The leading profile reproduces the disk density of states, while connected cumulants of a single master field encode the topological expansion. After formulating the cumulant power counting required by the topological expansion, we show that the cumulants reproduce all genus-zero multi-boundary amplitudes $\mathcal Z_{0,n}$. At higher genus, we show that a renormalization scheme can be chosen consistently order by order so that imposing one-boundary polynomiality recursively reproduces the perturbative JT string equation and yields the standard JT one-boundary amplitudes $\mathcal Z_{g,1}$. The framework provides a self-contained finite-$S_0$ quantum dynamics with a discrete spectrum and unitary real time evolution, beyond a mere rewriting of the matrix integral. The same confining dynamics also underlies late-time saturation and the dynamical avoidance of the would-be black hole singularity, as shown in our earlier work.

AI.tldr: Perturbative JT gravity is recast as an ensemble of 1D Hamiltonians with a confining random potential; its cumulants reproduce the topological (genus) expansion and JT amplitudes, providing a self-contained finite-$S_0$ quantum dynamics with discrete spectrum and unitary evolution.

The motivation is to realize perturbative Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity as an ensemble of ordinary quantum-mechanical Hamiltonians, connecting the genus/topological expansion to cumulants of a master field and linking to late-time physics and singularity avoidance.

Identify a single master field whose leading profile gives the disk density of states, with connected cumulants encoding the topological expansion. Establish a cumulant power counting dictated by the topological expansion, then introduce a renormalization scheme chosen consistently order by order so that imposing one-boundary polynomiality recursively yields the perturbative JT string equation and the standard JT amplitudes.

At higher genus, the chosen renormalization scheme, combined with one-boundary polynomiality imposed recursively, reproduces the perturbative JT string equation and yields the standard JT one-boundary amplitudes \mathcal Z_{g,1}.
