title: Complete four-loop pressure of cold QED
summary: Extending the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of a cold and dense ultrarelativistic electron gas to next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) in the gauge coupling has remained an open problem since the classic N2LO result of Freedman and McLerran, published in 1977. Here, we present the full N3LO pressure, the first thermodynamic quantity determined to this order in a physical gauge theory. The pressure exhibits good perturbative convergence and weak renormalization-scale dependence even at sizable couplings, while a Bayesian analysis of missing higher-order contributions indicates uncertainties that can exceed those inferred from scale variation alone.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the full N3LO pressure of a cold, dense ultrarelativistic electron gas—the first thermodynamic quantity determined to this order in a physical gauge theory—resolving a problem open since Freedman and McLerran's 1977 N2LO result.
AI.motivation: The weak-coupling expansion of the pressure for a cold, dense ultrarelativistic electron gas had stalled at N2LO since 1977. Advancing to N3LO was an open problem, and determining a thermodynamic quantity at this order in a physical gauge theory had not previously been achieved.
AI.method: The authors extend the weak-coupling (gauge-coupling) expansion of the pressure to next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO), computing the complete N3LO contribution to the pressure.
AI.result: The full N3LO pressure is obtained. It shows good perturbative convergence and weak renormalization-scale dependence even at sizable couplings. A Bayesian analysis of missing higher-order contributions yields uncertainties that can exceed those inferred from scale variation alone.
AI.conclusion: The N3LO pressure constitutes the first thermodynamic quantity determined to this order in a physical gauge theory, and its Bayesian uncertainty estimate suggests scale variation alone may underestimate the true theoretical error.

title: Codimension-Zero Holographic Complexity and Spectral Three-Point Correlators
summary: Holographic complexity is expected to capture the linear growth of black hole interiors, with quantum corrections ultimately leading to a late-time saturation. We develop a spectral formulation of holographic complexity measures associated with codimension-zero bulk regions in the framework of the complexity=anything proposal. The corresponding generating function of complexity is governed by three-point correlation functions of the density of states, establishing a direct connection between bulk geometric observables and nonperturbative Euclidean spacetime wormholes. We find that the codimension-zero holographic complexity reduces to the sum of two codimension-one contributions and exhibits a universal time evolution, characterized by an exponentially long regime of linear growth followed by saturation at the Heisenberg time. The late-time plateau is a direct result of the spectral level repulsion, a generic feature of quantum chaotic systems, thereby providing a universal mechanism for the saturation of holographic complexity. We also develop a complementary operator interpretation, in which Euclidean wormhole corrections render the semiclassical basis of fixed-complexity states overcomplete. Constructing a complete orthonormal basis then yields well-defined holographic complexity operators that reproduce the same universal time evolution. Our results establish a unified connection among black hole interiors, chaotic spectral statistics, and Euclidean wormholes in quantum gravity.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a spectral formulation of codimension-zero holographic complexity within the complexity=anything proposal, linking bulk geometry to Euclidean wormholes and chaotic spectral statistics, and shows a universal time evolution: long linear growth followed by saturation at the Heisenberg time.
AI.motivation: Holographic complexity is expected to capture the linear growth of black hole interiors, with quantum corrections eventually causing late-time saturation. The paper aims to provide a unified framework connecting black hole interiors, chaotic spectral statistics, and Euclidean wormholes, and to explain the mechanism behind the saturation of holographic complexity.

The generating function of complexity is expressed via three-point correlation functions of the density of states, relating bulk geometric observables to nonperturbative Euclidean spacetime wormholes. They also develop a complementary operator interpretation where Euclidean wormhole corrections make the semiclassical basis of fixed-complexity states overcomplete, and construct a complete orthonormal basis yielding well-defined complexity operators.

The late-time plateau arises from spectral level repulsion, a generic feature of quantum chaotic systems. The operator construction reproduces the same universal time evolution.
AI.conclusion: The results establish a unified connection among black hole interiors, chaotic spectral statistics, and Euclidean wormholes in quantum gravity, providing a universal mechanism—spectral level repulsion—for the saturation of holographic complexity.

title: Precision Tokenization for Multi-Modal Data in High Energy Physics
summary: Foundation models have recently gained significant attention in fields such as high energy physics (HEP). The tokenizers that convert detector data into discrete inputs for such models, however, are comparatively unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by learning discrete and compressed tokenized representations of HEP datasets. We demonstrate the approach on four modalities covering two different simulated detectors that vary in complexity. Treating tokenization as a rate-distortion problem, a systematic hyperparameter scan yields four design rules for tokenizing HEP data that hold across all set-based modalities studied. The cost of tokenization is evaluated on tasks including jet $p_T$ regression, particle flow reconstruction, and flavor tagging. We find that tokenization preserves much of the information needed for these tasks at compression factors of approximately 4-11$\times$ while keeping the jet $p_T$ resolution below 1%. We also present heptokens, an open-source library for tokenizing HEP data.

AI.tldr: This paper learns discrete, compressed tokenized representations of HEP detector data for foundation models, derives four design rules via a rate-distortion hyperparameter scan, evaluates tokenization cost on several downstream tasks, and releases an open-source library, heptokens.
AI.motivation: Foundation models are gaining traction in high energy physics (HEP), but the tokenizers that convert detector data into discrete inputs remain comparatively unexplored. This work addresses that gap.
AI.method: Tokenization is framed as a rate-distortion problem. A systematic hyperparameter scan is performed across four modalities from two simulated detectors of varying complexity, all set-based, yielding four design rules for tokenizing HEP data.
AI.result: Tokenization preserves much of the information needed for downstream tasks at compression factors of roughly 4-11x while keeping jet p_T resolution below 1%. Evaluated on jet p_T regression, particle flow reconstruction, and flavor tagging. The heptokens open-source library is released.
AI.conclusion: Discrete, compressed tokenizers can effectively serve HEP foundation models, with generalizable design rules and modest information loss, supported by an open-source tool.

title: General relativity and its modifications as effective field theories of $GL(4)$ breaking
summary: We discuss General Relativity and some of its modifications as effective field theories of the breaking of the affine general linear group using the coset approach and the Maurer-Cartan form. While the ultimate goal is to break the symmetry down to the Lorentz subgroup, we argue that there are three interesting breaking cascades in which the affine general linear group is first broken to a larger subgroup that contains the Lorentz group. In all cases, the breaking of translations always generates Goldstone modes that can be interpreted as metric degrees of freedom. We argue that the effective field theories that emerge as a result of the different breaking patterns are all dynamically equivalent at the lowest order of the derivative expansion, e.g., using Einstein-Hilbert-like actions, but can differ beyond the leading order.

AI.tldr: General Relativity and its modifications are treated as effective field theories from breaking the affine general linear group via the coset approach and Maurer-Cartan form; different breaking cascades yield metric degrees of freedom and dynamically equivalent leading-order theories.
AI.motivation: To understand General Relativity and its modifications as effective field theories arising from spontaneous symmetry breaking of the affine general linear group down to the Lorentz subgroup, and to explore viable intermediate breaking cascades.
AI.method: Coset approach and the Maurer-Cartan form are used to construct effective field theories based on breaking the affine general linear group, considering three breaking cascades where it is first broken to a larger subgroup containing the Lorentz group before the final breaking to Lorentz.
AI.result: The breaking of translations always generates Goldstone modes interpretable as metric degrees of freedom. The effective field theories from different breaking patterns are dynamically equivalent at the lowest order of the derivative expansion (e.g., Einstein-Hilbert-like actions) but differ beyond leading order.
AI.conclusion: General Relativity and its modifications can be unified as effective field theories of affine general linear group breaking, with distinct breaking cascades sharing leading-order dynamics but diverging at higher orders in the derivative expansion.

title: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
summary: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale Kähler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.

AI.tldr: The LZ 248 keV recoil can be explained by pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic Z interaction, realized in the MRSSM via an R-symmetric Dirac bino (supplying the Z transition) plus wino coannihilation (setting the relic abundance), with N=2 SUSY boundary conditions at a high scale.
AI.motivation: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate can be interpreted as pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic Z interaction, but in the MSSM the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound and a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy, so a new realization of such spectra is needed.
AI.method: Realize the required spectrum in the MRSSM, where an R-symmetric Dirac bino provides the Z transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance; impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of N=2 supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy; explore anomaly mediation for the Majorana splitting and a five-dimensional warped construction with Goldberger-Wise stabilization plus a loop correction to the no-scale Kähler potential.
AI.result: With remaining model parameters held fixed, spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV are obtained that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current; if anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV, and the warped construction generates this scale.
AI.conclusion: The MRSSM with N=2 boundary conditions yields viable pseudo-Dirac dark matter spectra for the LZ recoil; the spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos, and long-lived charged states.

title: On the quantum statistical relation and the covariant phase space Hamiltonian
summary: We show how the covariant phase space Hamiltonian can be constructed in theories in which some of the fields have gauge freedoms. The addition to the action of boundary terms that guarantee the well-posedness of a variational principle and its exact gauge invariance for the prescribed boundary conditions turn out to be essential in this construction. The same ingredients are essential in the use of the action in the framework of Gibbons and Hawking's Euclidean approach to Quantum Gravity and we show how the on-shell action constructed with a Lagrangian with those properties can be expressed in terms of the covariant phase space Hamiltonian. We compute the Hamiltonian of several theories, one of which has Chern--Simons terms, using our prescription and show that, in black-hole backgrounds, the Hamiltonian gives directly the quantum statistical relation including terms related to non-gravitational charges and chemical potentials, as expected.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs the covariant phase space Hamiltonian for gauge theories by including boundary terms that ensure a well-posed variational principle and exact gauge invariance, and shows the on-shell Euclidean action can be expressed via this Hamiltonian.
AI.motivation: In theories with gauge freedoms, constructing the covariant phase space Hamiltonian and using the action in Gibbons–Hawking's Euclidean quantum gravity approach is delicate, because the variational principle must be well-posed and gauge invariant. Boundary terms are essential but their role in this construction needed clarification.
AI.method: The authors add boundary terms to the action that guarantee a well-posed variational principle and exact gauge invariance for the prescribed boundary conditions. Using these ingredients, they build the covariant phase space Hamiltonian and relate the on-shell Euclidean action (constructed from a Lagrangian with these properties) to that Hamiltonian. They then compute the Hamiltonian for several theories, including one with Chern–Simons terms, and evaluate it in black-hole backgrounds.
AI.result: The on-shell action built from a Lagrangian with the required boundary properties can be expressed in terms of the covariant phase space Hamiltonian. In black-hole backgrounds, the computed Hamiltonian directly yields the quantum statistical relation, including contributions from non-gravitational charges and chemical potentials, as expected.
AI.conclusion: Boundary terms ensuring a well-posed, gauge-invariant variational principle are essential both for constructing the covariant phase space Hamiltonian and for the Euclidean quantum gravity framework. The resulting Hamiltonian provides a direct route to the quantum statistical relation in black-hole backgrounds.

title: Dualities, symmetries and the elliptic genus of 2d (0,2) SCFTs
summary: While naively simpler than its higher dimensional cousins, 2d physics still has its own share of puzzles. An example of this is instances of dualities of $(0,2)$ theories, passing all consistency checks save for a mismatch in global symmetry. This is common when said duality can be motivated by dimensional reduction of a duality of 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ theories where said symmetry emerges in 2d, often from an anomalous 4d symmetry. It is commonly believed that these symmetries are broken in the 2d theory, though often the mechanism for such breaking is not understood. We examine various appearances of this phenomenon and show that in these cases the elliptic genus shows signs of the presence of marginal operators that can break these symmetries. Interestingly, these operators do not appear perturbatively but emerge from the calculation, raising the question of what operators the $(0,2)$ elliptic genus actually counts. This provides a potential mechanism to overcome the discrepancy in symmetry, though we point out some potential subtleties.

AI.tldr: This paper studies 2d (0,2) dualities that pass all consistency checks except for a global symmetry mismatch, arguing that the elliptic genus reveals marginal operators that can break the "missing" symmetries.
AI.motivation: Dualities of 2d (0,2) theories often appear consistent but exhibit a mismatch in global symmetry, typically arising when the duality descends from a 4d N=1 duality under dimensional reduction and the relevant symmetry emerges in 2d from an anomalous 4d symmetry. Although these symmetries are commonly assumed to be broken in the 2d theory, the breaking mechanism is generally not understood. The paper aims to identify such a mechanism.
AI.method: The authors examine various appearances of this phenomenon in 2d (0,2) dualities and analyze the elliptic genus, looking for signatures of marginal operators capable of breaking the discrepant global symmetries. They assess whether these operators appear perturbatively or only emerge non-perturbatively from the genus computation.
AI.result: In the cases studied, the elliptic genus exhibits signs of marginal operators that can break the symmetries in question. Notably, these operators do not appear perturbatively but emerge from the calculation itself, which raises the question of what operators the (0,2) elliptic genus actually counts.
AI.conclusion: The emergence of these non-perturbative marginal operators provides a potential mechanism to resolve the global symmetry discrepancy between dual (0,2) theories. However, the authors point out some potential subtleties, including interpretive questions about the operator content counted by the elliptic genus.

title: Integrable auxiliary field sigma model and the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations
summary: We describe a family of two-dimensional metric deformations that preserve integrability. The seeds are (classically) conformal integrable field theories and the deformations are directly related to different classes of auxiliary field sigma models. We introduce a master action connecting deformations by Lie-algebra-valued auxiliary fields, the so-called $ν$-frame, to deformations by two Lorentz-charged scalars. These auxiliary scalar fields can be identified as Beltrami differentials of an auxiliary two-dimensional metric, providing a direct connection with the metric approach to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations. For Weyl-invariant seed matter theories, the auxiliary metric sector is described by a reduced gravitational potential. We show that the resulting framework preserves classical Lax integrability whenever the seed matter theory admits a Lax representation of its equations of motion on a generic curved two-dimensional spacetime. Finally, within the Lorentz-invariant family and the zweibein deformations of conformal matter theories considered here, we identify $T\bar{T}$ as the only deformation that can be interpreted as a field-dependent coordinate transformation.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a family of two-dimensional metric deformations of conformal integrable field theories, linked to auxiliary field sigma models, and shows integrability is preserved under a Lax representation condition, identifying $T\bar{T}$ as the unique field-dependent coordinate transformation.
AI.motivation: To unify and generalize $T\bar{T}$-like deformations by connecting auxiliary field deformations (the $\nu$-frame) with the metric approach, and to understand which deformations preserve classical integrability and admit a geometric interpretation.
AI.method: A master action is constructed connecting deformations by Lie-algebra-valued auxiliary fields ($\nu$-frame) to deformations by two Lorentz-charged scalars, identified as Beltrami differentials of an auxiliary two-dimensional metric. For Weyl-invariant seed matter, the auxiliary metric sector reduces to a gravitational potential. Classical Lax integrability is verified under the condition that the seed matter theory admits a Lax representation on a generic curved 2D spacetime.
AI.result: The framework preserves classical Lax integrability whenever the seed matter theory admits a Lax representation on a generic curved two-dimensional spacetime. Within the Lorentz-invariant family and zweibein deformations of conformal matter, $T\bar{T}$ is identified as the only deformation interpretable as a field-dependent coordinate transformation.
AI.conclusion: The master action provides a unified description linking auxiliary-field and metric approaches to $T\bar{T}$-like deformations, with integrability preservation guaranteed by the seed theory's Lax structure, and singles out $T\bar{T}$ as the unique field-dependent coordinate transformation among the deformations studied.

title: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames
summary: We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.

AI.tldr: Krylov complexity in confined holographic QCD depends sensitively on probe type (particle vs. string) and frame (Einstein vs. string), with particles distinguishing the two confining geometries in the Einstein frame while strings yield oscillatory behavior in both.
AI.motivation: Krylov complexity has emerged as a probe of operator growth and quantum chaos, and a recent correspondence links its growth rate to the proper radial momentum of probes falling into the bulk. The authors aim to test this correspondence in confining holographic QCD backgrounds, where the dynamics of confinement and IR physics are subtle, and to assess whether Krylov complexity can distinguish different confining geometries.
AI.method: Using the correspondence between Krylov complexity growth rate and the proper radial momentum of bulk probes, the authors study two horizonless confining backgrounds from an Einstein-dilaton gravity system: the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime. They compute Krylov complexity for massive particles in the Einstein frame, then analyze string dynamics in the string frame, and finally revisit massive-particle dynamics in the string frame.
AI.result: In the Einstein frame, particle Krylov complexity differs qualitatively between the two backgrounds: it oscillates periodically in the deformed AdS-soliton (with parameter-dependent period and amplitude) but grows exponentially at late times without oscillations in deformed thermal-AdS. In the string frame, string Krylov complexity oscillates in both backgrounds, traced to an additional turning point emerging in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Massive-particle dynamics in the string frame show qualitatively similar behavior in both backgrounds.
AI.conclusion: The Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on both the choice of probe and the frame. Working in the string frame reveals a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries, whereas the Einstein-frame particle analysis distinguishes them.

title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
summary: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ and $Δ=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

AI.tldr: This paper studies anomaly-induced transport in a holographic superconductor with spontaneous symmetry breaking, finding that the condensate causes anomaly-induced effects to leak into the non-anomalous sector, independent of scalar quantization.
AI.motivation: Anomaly-induced transport (e.g., chiral magnetic conductivity) is typically associated with anomalous currents. The authors ask whether spontaneous symmetry breaking in a superconducting phase can extend these effects beyond the anomalous sector and whether the result depends on the choice of scalar field quantization.
AI.method: A holographic model in the probe limit with vector and axial gauge fields, an extra non-anomalous U(1) symmetry, and a charged scalar driving the transition. Superconducting backgrounds are constructed numerically for two scalar quantizations, corresponding to operators of scaling dimension Δ=1 and Δ=3 (O1 and O2 theories). Chiral magnetic conductivities are computed via Kubo formulae and compared with analytical limits for Oi→0 and Oi→∞.
AI.result: Spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly affecting the non-anomalous sector as well. This effect occurs in both the O1 and O2 theories, showing independence from the chosen scalar quantization. Numerical results match the analytical limits for Oi→0 and Oi→∞ in both theories.
AI.conclusion: Anomaly-induced transport is not confined to anomalous currents once symmetry breaking occurs; it also permeates the non-anomalous sector. This behavior is robust against the scalar field quantization, with consistent numerical and analytical agreement across both O1 and O2 theories.

title: Robustness of exact $SU(N)$ Einstein-Skyrme solutions: black holes, wormholes and cosmologies
summary: The $SU(2)$ Skyrme model admits exact solutions when coupled to General Relativity in four spacetime dimensions. Here, we demonstrate that relevant gravitational configurations, such as black holes, wormholes, and cosmologies, are robust under the extension to $SU(N)$ with an arbitrary number of flavors. We show that key physical features, such as the thermodynamic properties, the baryon number of the configurations, and the geometry, are crucially determined by the number of flavors as well as the coupling constants of the theory. In particular: first, we prove that an increase in the matter content favors the local thermal stability of spherically symmetric black holes. Second, for cosmological solutions, we demonstrate analytically that as the hadronic matter content increases, the scale factor grows more slowly due to enhanced gravitational attraction, while the expansion rate (measured by the Hubble parameter) increases as a consequence of the higher energy density. Third, we find that the throat of traversable wormhole solutions can be enlarged by increasing the number of flavors, since the energy density required to keep the throat open does not grow indefinitely but rather saturates at a finite value.

AI.tldr: The paper generalizes the $SU(2)$ Skyrme model coupled to General Relativity to $SU(N)$ with arbitrary flavors, showing that black holes, wormholes, and cosmological solutions remain robust and that their physical properties depend crucially on the number of flavors and coupling constants.
AI.motivation: Exact solutions of the $SU(2)$ Skyrme model coupled to General Relativity are known in four spacetime dimensions, but it is unclear whether such gravitational configurations (black holes, wormholes, cosmologies) persist and how their properties change when the model is extended to $SU(N)$ with an arbitrary number of flavors.
AI.method: The authors extend the $SU(2)$ Skyrme model to $SU(N)$ with an arbitrary number of flavors coupled to General Relativity, and analyze the resulting gravitational configurations analytically, examining thermodynamic properties, baryon number, and geometry as functions of flavor number and coupling constants.
AI.result: The analysis yields three key findings: (i) increasing the matter content favors local thermal stability of spherically symmetric black holes; (ii) for cosmological solutions, increasing hadronic matter content slows the scale factor growth due to enhanced gravitational attraction while the Hubble parameter increases from higher energy density; (iii) the throat of traversable wormholes can be enlarged by increasing flavor number, since the energy density required to keep the throat open saturates at a finite value rather than growing indefinitely.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational configurations—black holes, wormholes, and cosmologies—are robust under the extension of the Skyrme model to $SU(N)$ with arbitrary flavors, with their thermodynamic, topological (baryon number), and geometric features controlled by the number of flavors and the coupling constants.

title: Dynamical symmetry breaking in a non-polynomial four-fermion model
summary: We present a new four-fermion model with a strongly non-polynomial coupling. To eliminate these non-polynomialities, we introduce two auxiliary vector fields and show that the dynamical Lorentz symmetry breaking is possible in our theory, as revealed by the effective potential generated for these vector fields. We explicitly calculate the low-energy effective action for these fields, which is given by the sum of three Maxwell terms (one for each field and a mixed one) plus a potential term displaying nontrivial minima.

AI.tldr: A four-fermion model with strongly non-polynomial coupling is reformulated via two auxiliary vector fields, and the generated effective potential for these fields allows dynamical Lorentz symmetry breaking, with a low-energy effective action consisting of three Maxwell terms plus a potential with nontrivial minima.
AI.motivation: The strongly non-polynomial coupling in the proposed four-fermion model obstructs direct analysis, motivating the introduction of auxiliary fields to render the theory tractable and to investigate whether dynamical Lorentz symmetry breaking can occur.
AI.method: Two auxiliary vector fields are introduced to eliminate the non-polynomialities of the four-fermion coupling. The effective potential generated for these vector fields is then analyzed, and the low-energy effective action for the vector fields is explicitly computed.
AI.result: The effective potential develops nontrivial minima, indicating that dynamical Lorentz symmetry breaking is possible. The explicit low-energy effective action is the sum of three Maxwell terms—one for each vector field plus a mixed term—together with the potential term exhibiting nontrivial minima.
AI.conclusion: The theory admits dynamical Lorentz symmetry breaking, and its low-energy regime is governed by a Maxwell-like effective action with a nontrivial potential for the auxiliary vector fields.

title: G2 resolutions and backtracking in scale-separated AdS$_3$
summary: We study scale-separated AdS$_3$ models with full moduli stabilization in massive IIA supergravity on G2 orientifolds. In addition to constructing new examples, we investigate the properties of these models once the singularities of the G2 toroidal orbifold are resolved. The blow-up moduli are shown to be stabilized using fluxes in a parametric regime that preserves scale separation and control under the supergravity approximation. We further show that the apparent orientifold intersections in the singular orbifold description do not exist on such resolved spaces. Finally, we analyze the brane dual picture of such models using flux backtracking. We highlight several interesting features from such analysis such as a finite interval solution of the resulting flow equations in some of the models and the desirable low-energy decoupling of brane modes.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs scale-separated AdS3 vacua with full moduli stabilization in massive IIA supergravity on G2 orientifolds, studies their fate after resolving orbifold singularities, shows blow-up moduli can be stabilized while preserving scale separation and control, demonstrates that apparent orientifold intersections vanish on resolved spaces, and analyzes the brane dual via flux backtracking, finding finite-interval flow solutions and low-energy decoupling of brane modes.
AI.motivation: Scale-separated AdS vacua with fully stabilized moduli are central to holography and to connecting string theory to lower-dimensional effective theories, yet constructing such models in massive IIA on G2 orientifolds and understanding their behavior at singularities remains challenging. The work aims to move beyond singular orbifold descriptions to resolved geometries and to test whether scale separation and supergravity control survive, while also probing the dual brane/field-theory picture.
AI.method: The authors work in massive IIA supergravity on G2 orientifolds, construct new scale-separated AdS3 examples, resolve the singularities of the toroidal G2 orbifold, and stabilize the resulting blow-up moduli using fluxes in a parametric regime that maintains scale separation and supergravity control. They examine the orientifold intersections present in the singular description versus the resolved space, and perform flux backtracking to derive the brane dual and its flow equations.
AI.result: New scale-separated AdS3 models with full moduli stabilization are constructed. Blow-up moduli are stabilized by fluxes while preserving scale separation and supergravity control. The apparent orientifold intersections of the singular orbifold do not exist on the resolved spaces. The brane dual analysis via flux backtracking exhibits a finite-interval solution of the flow equations in some models and desirable low-energy decoupling of brane modes.
AI.conclusion: Resolving G2 orbifold singularities yields consistent scale-separated AdS3 vacua with fully stabilized moduli, eliminating spurious orientifold intersections and allowing controlled flux stabilization of blow-up modes. The dual brane description reinforces the viability of these models through finite-interval flows and low-energy decoupling, supporting their use in holographic and phenomenological contexts.

title: The Gregory-Laflamme Instability of five-dimensional Black Strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
summary: We complement and extend our recent study of the non-linear evolution of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five spacetime dimensions. First, we study time-dependent perturbations of uniform black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory and determine the growth rates as a function of the coupling. We find that for positive Gauss-Bonnet couplings, the black strings are more unstable than in general relativity in the sense that the growth rates are larger and shorter wavelengths are unstable. In the second part of the paper we show that the hyperbolicity of the equation of motion of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory is determined by an effective metric when the dynamics is restricted to spherical symmetry in the asymptotically flat directions. When the effective field theory becomes strongly coupled, as it happens near the endpoint of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of the black string, this effective metric becomes degenerate and the Cauchy evolution breaks down. Applying this criterion to uniform black strings, we find that for any positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling there is an open set of regular solutions (including the one of minimal thickness) on which the effective metric degenerates in a neighbourhood of the horizon. Therefore, we argue that these solutions cannot be attained from weakly coupled initial data by Cauchy evolution and the solutions of the linearized equations around them cannot be interpreted as approximations to nearby non-linear evolutions. We provide further evidence for this picture with non-linear simulations of the Gregory-Laflamme instability. The non-linear simulations terminate through a loss of hyperbolicity of the Tricomi or Keldysh type, depending on the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling.

AI.tldr: This work extends the study of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) gravity in 5D: positive couplings enhance the instability, and at strong coupling the effective metric degenerates, causing loss of hyperbolicity and breakdown of Cauchy evolution.
AI.motivation: To complement and extend prior work on the non-linear evolution of the Gregory-Laflamme instability of black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five spacetime dimensions, and to understand how the Gauss-Bonnet coupling affects both the instability and the well-posedness of the evolution.
AI.method: Time-dependent perturbation analysis of uniform black strings in EGB theory to determine instability growth rates versus coupling; analysis of the hyperbolicity of the EGB equations of motion via an effective metric when dynamics is restricted to spherical symmetry in asymptotically flat directions; application of this criterion to uniform black strings; non-linear simulations of the Gregory-Laflamme instability.
AI.result: For positive Gauss-Bonnet couplings, black strings are more unstable than in general relativity: growth rates are larger and shorter wavelengths are unstable. The effective metric degenerates when the effective field theory becomes strongly coupled, as near the endpoint of the instability, breaking down Cauchy evolution. For any positive coupling there is an open set of regular solutions (including the minimal-thickness one) on which the effective metric degenerates near the horizon. Non-linear simulations terminate through loss of hyperbolicity of Tricomi or Keldysh type, depending on the sign of the coupling.
AI.conclusion: Black strings with positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling are more unstable than in GR, and strongly coupled regimes yield a degenerate effective metric that destroys hyperbolicity. Consequently, such solutions cannot be reached from weakly coupled initial data via Cauchy evolution, and linearized solutions around them do not approximate nearby non-linear evolutions.

title: A discrete analogue of $\mathscr{N}=2$ super Weil-Petersson volumes
summary: We introduce a discrete spectral curve from $\mathscr{N}=2$ double-scaled SYK whose topological recursion defines quasi-polynomial volumes in integer boundary lengths. The curve has two edge theories: a local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory at the lower edge and a bosonic theory at the upper edge. Focusing on the local $\mathscr{N}=2$ theory, we compute its finite-$q$ volumes and independently check the first few using the string equation. In the $q\rightarrow 1$ continuum limit, these recover the super Weil-Petersson volumes of Turiaci and Witten. Finally, we give an all-genus intersection-theoretic interpretation of these local volumes on the moduli space of stable marked curves, in terms of a deformed spin class with a gap-dependent $κ$-class dressing.

AI.tldr: A discrete spectral curve from N=2 double-scaled SYK is introduced; its topological recursion yields quasi-polynomial volumes, recovering super Weil-Petersson volumes in the q→1 limit and admitting an all-genus intersection-theoretic interpretation on moduli space.
AI.motivation: To connect discrete/holographic models (double-scaled SYK with N=2 supersymmetry) to the geometry of moduli spaces of curves, and to generalize known Weil-Petersson volumes (including the super version of Turiaci–Witten) to a finite-q, discrete setting.
AI.method: Construct a discrete spectral curve from N=2 double-scaled SYK with two edge theories (local N=2 at the lower edge, bosonic at the upper edge). Apply topological recursion to define quasi-polynomial volumes in integer boundary lengths. For the local N=2 theory, compute finite-q volumes, verify the first few via the string equation, and take the q→1 continuum limit. Provide an all-genus intersection-theoretic formulation on the moduli space of stable marked curves using a deformed spin class with gap-dependent κ-class dressing.
AI.result: Finite-q volumes for the local N=2 edge theory are obtained and cross-checked against the string equation. In the q→1 continuum limit these reproduce the super Weil-Petersson volumes of Turiaci and Witten. The volumes admit an all-genus intersection-theoretic interpretation on the moduli space of stable marked curves.
AI.conclusion: The discrete spectral curve and its topological recursion unify finite-q SYK-type volumes with super Weil-Petersson geometry, providing a deformed spin-class/κ-class intersection-theoretic description valid to all genera.

title: The Quasiparticle Ansatz for Relativistic Continuous Matrix Product States
summary: The Relativistic Continuous Matrix Product State (RCMPS) ansatz introduced in arXiv:2102.07741 is a translation-invariant variational ansatz intended to approximate the ground states of gapped one-dimensional relativistic Quantum Field Theories directly in the continuum limit and in infinite volume. In this work, we develop an ansatz, referred to as the Relativistic Quasiparticle (RQP) ansatz, for the low-lying one-particle excitations of the RCMPS vacuum, as well as for solitons interpolating between two distinct degenerate vacua. The corresponding energies of these states can be obtained as the eigenvalues of an effective Hamiltonian. The RQP ansatz generalizes constructions used in the Matrix Product State and Continuous Matrix Product State literature. We apply the RQP ansatz to the sine-Gordon model and find good agreement with results from integrability for both the soliton and breather masses. We also apply the RQP ansatz to the $φ^4$ theory, in both its $\mathbb Z_2$-preserving and $\mathbb{Z}_2$-broken phases, and determine the spectrum of particles and solitons. This enables us to determine the parameter regime for which multiple stable particles exist.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a Relativistic Quasiparticle (RQP) ansatz to describe low-lying one-particle excitations and solitons on top of the RCMPS vacuum, enabling spectral computations in continuum relativistic QFTs such as sine-Gordon and φ⁴.
AI.motivation: The RCMPS ansatz (arXiv:2102.07741) approximates gapped 1D relativistic QFT ground states directly in the continuum and infinite volume, but excited states—one-particle excitations and solitons—lacked a comparable variational construction.
AI.method: An RQP ansatz for low-lying one-particle excitations of the RCMPS vacuum and for solitons interpolating between degenerate vacua; energies obtained as eigenvalues of an effective Hamiltonian. Generalizes MPS/CMPS constructions, applied to sine-Gordon and φ⁴ (Z₂-preserving and Z₂-broken phases).
AI.result: For sine-Gordon, RQP results agree well with integrability for both soliton and breather masses. For φ⁴, the particle and soliton spectra are determined in both phases, identifying the parameter regime where multiple stable particles exist.
AI.conclusion: The RQP ansatz provides an effective variational framework for excited states and topological solitons in continuum relativistic QFTs, validated against integrable benchmarks and extended to characterize φ⁴ spectra and multi-particle stability regimes.

title: Modular Properties of Generalised Gibbs Ensembles: The Deformed KdV Hierarchy
summary: We construct a set of conserved charges which are deformations of quantum KdV charges. They are associated with the modular transformation of a GGE with the spin-$σ$ KdV charge inserted with chemical potential $α_σ$. The charges are formal power series in the chemical potential, with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. We define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of the currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. We show that the eigenvalues of these deformed charges can be obtained from the thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz in two models. In the $c=1/2$ free fermion theory, the deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues agree with the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, we find numerical agreement through cubic order in the spin-$5$ deformation for the first few charges evaluated on low-lying states.

AI.tldr: The authors construct deformed quantum KdV conserved charges (formal power series in chemical potential, coefficients = local integrals of motion), establish their commutativity/uniqueness, and verify their eigenvalues against the TBA in the c=1/2 free fermion and Lee-Yang models.
AI.motivation: Modular transformation of a Generalized Gibbs Ensemble (GGE) with a spin-σ KdV charge and chemical potential motivates a family of charges deforming quantum KdV charges; understanding these deformations and their eigenvalues is the goal.
AI.method: Construct deformed charges as formal power series in the chemical potential with coefficients given by local integrals of motion. Define local recursion relations and equivalent flow equations, prove commutativity to all orders, and establish uniqueness of currents modulo total derivatives for a fixed generating series. Compare eigenvalues with the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) in two models.
AI.result: In the c=1/2 free fermion theory, deformed charges reduce to explicit linear combinations of undeformed KdV charges, and their ground-state eigenvalues match the TBA expansion to all orders. In the Lee-Yang model, numerical agreement is found through cubic order in the spin-5 deformation for the first few charges on low-lying states.
AI.conclusion: The deformed charges form a consistent commutative family and their eigenvalues are accessible via TBA, with exact all-order agreement in the free fermion case and perturbative (cubic-order) agreement in the Lee-Yang model.

title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson Volumes from the Spectral Edge of DSSYK and Supersymmetric Extensions
summary: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same q-deformed volumes can be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to the $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call "irrelevant" contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how q-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that q-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes arise from a double-scaled matrix model obtained by zooming in on the spectral edges of DSSYK models, and uses this to construct candidate q-deformed N=1 super Weil-Petersson volumes.
AI.motivation: The q-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do–Norbury correspond to the top-degree part of Okuyama's discrete volumes defined via topological recursion on the DSSYK spectral curve. A more intuitive and constructive understanding of these volumes, and their extension to supersymmetric settings, was lacking.
AI.method: A double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is obtained by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density is used to reproduce the same q-deformed volumes. The same edge-zooming procedure is applied to the hard edge of N=1 DSSYK to define candidate q-deformed N=1 super Weil-Petersson volumes.
AI.result: The matrix-model construction reproduces the q-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes. The candidate N=1 super volumes are polynomials of fixed degree and reduce to the N=1 super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled q→1 limit; they differ from the Do–Norbury N=1 volumes (arXiv:2510.12431) only by "irrelevant" contributions that vanish in the scaled q→1 limit.
AI.conclusion: q-Deformed volumes can be naturally associated with the spectral edges of various DSSYK models, providing an intuitive way to construct them, including in supersymmetric contexts.

title: Reflected entropy and islands in JT gravity from partial dimensional reduction
summary: We study how mixed-state correlations reorganize across island transitions in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to a non-gravitating bath. Using the partial-dimensional-reduction realization of double holography, we compute reflected entropy for adjacent and disjoint radiation regions in the vacuum and in the thermofield-double state of an eternal black hole. Reflected entropy probes the internal partition of the entanglement wedge and therefore resolves structure that is invisible to the ordinary Page curve: its dominant saddle can change even when the entropy saddle of the union remains fixed, and it vanishes at leading order when the entanglement wedge disconnects. We show that the lower-dimensional reflected-island description agrees, to leading order in the dynamical brane fluctuation, with the higher-dimensional defect-extremal-surface picture. The finite-angle comparison further suggests a projection-covariant identification of island and brane endpoints at linear order. The resulting Page-like curves and Markov gaps provide a geometric probe of the reorganization of the purification and of non-Markovian, multipartite correlation structure during island transitions.

AI.tldr: This paper uses reflected entropy to track how mixed-state correlations reorganize across island transitions in JT gravity coupled to a bath, showing reflected entropy resolves entanglement-wedge structure invisible to the ordinary Page curve, and that the lower-dimensional reflected-island picture matches the higher-dimensional defect-extremal-surface description at leading order.
AI.motivation: Ordinary entanglement-entropy Page curves do not resolve the internal partition of the entanglement wedge during island transitions; a finer probe is needed to capture how purification and multipartite correlation structure reorganize.
AI.method: Working in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to a non-gravitating bath, the authors use the partial-dimensional-reduction realization of double holography to compute reflected entropy for adjacent and disjoint radiation regions in the vacuum and in the thermofield-double state of an eternal black hole. They compare the lower-dimensional reflected-island description with the higher-dimensional defect-extremal-surface picture, including a finite-angle analysis.
AI.result: The dominant reflected-entropy saddle can change even when the entropy saddle of the union stays fixed, and reflected entropy vanishes at leading order when the entanglement wedge disconnects. The lower-dimensional reflected-island description agrees with the higher-dimensional defect-extremal-surface picture to leading order in dynamical brane fluctuations; the finite-angle comparison suggests a projection-covariant identification of island and brane endpoints at linear order.
AI.conclusion: The resulting Page-like curves and Markov gaps yield a geometric probe of the reorganization of purification and of non-Markovian, multipartite correlation structure during island transitions.

title: A universal sector of $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ spectra
summary: We determine a universal sector of the spectrum of light operators in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ class $\mathcal{S}$ superconformal field theories arising from M5-branes wrapped on a compact hyperbolic Riemann surface $Σ_2$. We work at large $N$, analysing Kaluza--Klein fluctuations about the dual Bah--Beem--Bobev--Wecht anti-de Sitter backgrounds for general values of the twist parameter $z$. To obtain these spectra, we specialise recently derived mass operators to modes that are constant on $Σ_2$ by imposing a suitable $z$-dependent generalised $G$-structure. We then organise the resulting eigenstates into long and protected $\mathcal{N}=1$ supermultiplets with definite flavour quantum numbers. As $z$ varies, rich patterns emerge in the spectrum, including both isolated multiplets and infinite towers of multiplets, which we characterise analytically.

AI.tldr: The paper determines a universal sector of light operator spectra in 4D N=1 class S SCFTs from M5-branes on a hyperbolic Riemann surface, at large N, by analyzing KK fluctuations about BBBW AdS backgrounds and organizing eigenstates into N=1 supermultiplets with flavor quantum numbers.
AI.motivation: Understanding the spectrum of light operators in class S superconformal field theories is important for probing their dynamics and the holographic duality. Prior work lacked a systematic determination of this universal sector across general twist parameters.
AI.method: At large N, Kaluza-Klein fluctuations about the dual Bah-Beem-Bobev-Wecht AdS backgrounds are analyzed for general twist parameter z. Recently derived mass operators are specialized to modes constant on the Riemann surface by imposing a z-dependent generalized G-structure, and eigenstates are organized into long and protected N=1 supermultiplets with definite flavor quantum numbers.
AI.result: The resulting spectra exhibit rich patterns as z varies, including isolated multiplets and infinite towers of multiplets, all characterized analytically.
AI.conclusion: A universal sector of light operators in these class S theories is identified and fully characterized, revealing z-dependent structure of isolated and tower-like multiplets.

title: Effective field theory for strong phase transitions
summary: We show how to construct perturbative effective field theories for strong phase transitions, where the standard tools of high-temperature dimensional reduction fail. By identifying the relevant power counting relations for the couplings, masses and background fields, we construct a controlled perturbative expansion adapted to this regime. We find that the order parameter field remains light at the transition, so that there is a controlled derivative expansion, even though large external fields need to be resummed. The resulting effective field theories for strong phase transitions live in three dimensions and have nonpolynomial field dependence. Applying our framework to a two-scalar model, we verify renormalisation scale cancellation through next-to-next-to-leading order and find decreasing corrections to the latent heat as the perturbative order is increased. Extending to include fermions and gauge fields, we identify a broad class of models in which strong-transition thermodynamics are systematically improvable.

AI.tldr: The paper develops perturbative effective field theories for strong phase transitions where standard high-temperature dimensional reduction breaks down, by identifying proper power counting and constructing a controlled 3D derivative expansion with nonpolynomial field dependence.
AI.motivation: Standard high-temperature dimensional reduction fails for strong phase transitions, so a new controlled perturbative framework is needed to describe their thermodynamics.
AI.method: Identify relevant power counting relations for couplings, masses, and background fields; construct a controlled perturbative expansion, noting the order parameter remains light and permits a derivative expansion despite large external fields needing resummation; build 3D effective field theories with nonpolynomial field dependence.
AI.result: In a two-scalar model, renormalisation scale cancellation verified through NNLO, with decreasing corrections to latent heat as perturbative order increases; extended to fermions and gauge fields, identifying a broad class of models with systematically improvable strong-transition thermodynamics.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides a systematic, improvable perturbative treatment of strong phase transition thermodynamics, applicable to a broad class of models including fermions and gauge fields.
